name: agentflow
description: Fan out work to many agents via a workflow script — parallel subagent orchestration with journaled results and resume. Use when a task needs >4 independent agent calls, staged phases with aggregation, or results too large to keep in your own context.
---

# Agentflow — script-driven multi-agent orchestration

You orchestrate turn-by-turn by default: every subagent result lands in your
context window. Agentflow moves the loop, branching, and intermediate results
into a JavaScript file that a runner executes — you keep only the final answer.

## When to use

- Fan-out beyond ~4 independent agent calls (file-per-file reviews, repo-wide
  audits, per-endpoint checks, N-variant drafting).
- Staged pipelines where later phases consume earlier results.
- Runs you may need to interrupt and resume.
- Results are bulky: the script holds them; you read the synthesis.

## When NOT to use

- 1-4 subagent calls — just use your harness's native subagent tool; a CLI
  session per call has real startup cost, so keep fan-out granularity
  meaningful (a whole file audit, not a function rename).
- Anything needing shared state, locks, or transactions between agents —
  workflow agents share nothing but the filesystem.
- Claude Code's **native** Workflow tool (ultracode/`/deep-research`) — inside
  Claude sessions, prefer it; it is faster and cheaper than spawning `claude -p`.

## How it works

```bash
agentflow run workflow.mjs --harness devin --concurrency 8
agentflow run workflow.mjs --resume <run-id>   # after interrupt
agentflow doctor                             # check harness availability
```

Each `agent()` call spawns one **non-interactive CLI session** of the selected
harness as a subprocess, in a fresh context, and resolves to `{text, json}` or
`null` on failure. Calls queue under a bounded concurrency pool (default 8).
Every settled call is journaled to `.agentflow/runs/<run-id>.jsonl` with a
fingerprint of its prompt/model/schema/context; `--resume` replays records
whose fingerprint still matches and re-executes only what never finished or
changed since the run (logs `replay miss [i]` — stale results can't surface).

## Workflow script contract

`.mjs` file, top-level `await` allowed, globals injected:

| Global | Signature | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `agent` | `(prompt, opts?) => Promise<{text, json, usage?} \| null>` | opts: `label`, `model`, `schema`, `worktree`, `cwd`, `timeout` (ms), `permission`, `retries`, `schemaRetries`. With `schema`, the parsed JSON is validated against a JSON Schema subset and re-prompted with the error up to `schemaRetries` times (default 4, so 5 attempts total). `usage` is `{promptTokens, completionTokens, cachedTokens, steps}` when the harness reports it — **devin only** today (from `--export` final_metrics); also journaled and summed by `status`/`watch` |
| `parallel` | `(thunks) => Promise<results>` | `parallel(files.map(f => () => agent(...)))` — order preserved, `null` per failure |
| `pipeline` | `(items, ...stages) => Promise<results>` | each item flows through stages; `null` short-circuits that item |
| `batch` | `(items, opts?) => Promise<results>` | async fan-out on **openrouter** (one OR Batch job per N prompts, ~40–60% off, ≤24h window), **devin** (N cloud sessions — `devin_mode` model, `structured_output` collected; swe-2 models are free), **perplexity** (N `/v1/async/sonar` requests — async accepts **`sonar-deep-research` only**), **openai** (Batches API, ~50% off, 24h) or **anthropic** (Message Batches, ~50% off, 24h). Items: `{prompt, label?, model?, schema?, maxTokens?}`; all share ONE model (`opts.model` or per-item). opts: `batchPollMs` (15s), `batchTimeoutMs` (2h). Results align to input order; each item consumes a normal call index |
| `phase` | `(name) => void` | labels stderr progress; journaled so `watch`/`tail` group lanes by phase |
| `log` | `(msg) => void` | stderr; keep secrets out |
| `args` | any | string array after `--` on the CLI, or parsed JSON via `--args-json` (e.g. `--args-json '{"task":"x","n":3}'` — Claude-parity structured args) |
| `cwd` | string | the run's working directory (matches `--cwd` default) — use for `node:fs` paths in scripts |
| `meta` | object | from `export const meta = {...}` |

Script ends with `return <value>` → the value prints on **stdout** (progress
stays stderr, so `agentflow run w.mjs > out.json` composes) and is journaled
on `run-end`. `process.exit(code)` inside a script ends the *script* with
that code — it can never kill the runner (Claude's sandbox parity).
Claude-parity gap: `stallMs` (inactivity timeout per agent) isn't implemented —
`timeout` is a hard wall-clock kill, the documented subset is `return` +
`args` + `process.exit`.

Constraints:

- `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` is the only export; it
  must be a **plain object literal**. `phases` is an array of phase-name
  strings matching your `phase()` calls (parity with Claude's native contract).
- No static `import`/`export` — scripts are self-contained. Dynamic
  `await import('node:fs')` works.
- Determinism is your job: the fingerprint guard stops stale results from
  replaying, but reordered/inserted calls still cascade re-executions — keep
  `agent()` call order stable across runs (don't drive it off `Date.now()`
  or unordered directory listings).

## Per-harness adapter table

| `--harness` | Spawns | `model` | `schema` | `worktree` | `permission: 'escalated'` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devin` (default) | `devin -p` | `--model` (e.g. `claude-haiku-5-5-low`, `adaptive`) | prompt-level JSON instruction | planned | `dangerous` |
| `claude` | `claude -p --output-format json` | `--model` | prompt-level | no | `bypassPermissions` |
| `codex` | `codex exec` | `-m` | native `--output-schema` | `--worktree` | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` |
| `opencode` | `opencode run --format json` | `-m provider/model` | prompt-level | no | `--auto` |
| `ori` | `ori code -p` | `--model <openrouter-slug>` — any model on OpenRouter | prompt-level | no | `self-drive` (binary approval surface; `manual` stalls headless) |
| `openrouter` | in-process `POST /chat/completions` — **no subprocess, no tools** | OR slug (default `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`) | prompt-level | n/a | n/a — needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in env |
| `perplexity` | in-process `POST /chat/completions` — grounded answers + `citations` | `sonar` (default), `sonar-pro`; **batch: `sonar-deep-research` only** | prompt-level | n/a | n/a — needs `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` in env |
| `openai` | in-process `POST /v1/chat/completions` — **no subprocess, no tools** | OpenAI slug (default `gpt-4.1-mini`) | prompt-level | n/a | n/a — needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` in env |
| `anthropic` | in-process `POST /v1/messages` — **no subprocess, no tools** | Anthropic slug (default `claude-haiku-4-5`) | prompt-level | n/a | n/a — needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in env |
| `echo` | none (test adapter) | — | canned | — | — |

`openrouter` is the cheapest surface — use it for tool-free stages
(decompose, classify, verify prose, synthesize); harness adapters only where
agents need the filesystem. For latency-tolerant volume, `batch(items)`
runs the harness's async-jobs surface instead of N sync calls — the run
polls until done (interrupt mid-poll is safe: `--resume` re-polls the same
journaled ids, never resubmits). On openrouter that's one `/batches` job
(model must be batch-capable); on devin it's one Cloud session per item
(`structured_output` is the result channel, sessions idle at
`waiting_for_user` once produced — that is the completion signal); on
perplexity it's one async sonar request per item (`COMPLETED` + `response`
— grounded answers carry `citations` through to the result); on
openai it's a JSONL file upload + one `/v1/batches` job; on anthropic one
`/v1/messages/batches` call (`max_tokens` required — default 8192, per-item
`maxTokens` overrides).

**`--via ori`** wraps workers in Ori's OpenRouter environment
(`ori claude -p ...`) — the harness keeps its own flags and parsing, but
credentials and `model:` values route through OpenRouter (`model:
'x-ai/grok-4-fast'`, `deepseek/...`, etc.). Ori consumes `--model` and
`--reasoning-effort` itself in wrapper mode — `agent(..., {
reasoningEffort: 'high' })` translates to the harness's native mechanism.
Wrappable harnesses: claude, codex, opencode, grok, kilo, hermes, cline, pi,
muse, omp, prime-agent — no devin launcher exists. Requires `ori` on PATH;
`--via` on the CLI or `via: 'ori'` in `agentflow.json` applies to every
`agent()` call; a call can opt out with `via: 'direct'`.

**`worktree: 'auto'`** gives the call its own git checkout — the runner runs
`git worktree add --detach` under `.agentflow/worktrees/` and sets that call's
`cwd` there (journaled as a `worktree` record). Use it when file-mutating
agents would collide in one checkout. `'auto'` is runner-owned and consumed
before the adapter sees the spec; `worktree: true` still passes through to
adapter-native flags (codex `--worktree`). Worktrees deliberately persist
after the run — `agentflow clean` reclaims them for ended runs (`--all` also
sweeps unrecorded dirs under `.agentflow/worktrees/`).

Default permission postures are least-privilege (`smart` devin / `auto` claude /
`workspace-write` codex / none opencode). Headless agents that hit an approval
prompt fail with `permissionDenied` journaled — prefer widening the prompt or
`permission: 'escalated'` over re-running blindly.

## Cost discipline

Every harness `agent()` is a full session — real tokens plus seconds of
startup; `openrouter` adapter calls are a single completion (~$0.01–0.05).
Measured numbers and per-model tables: `docs/research/orchestration-economics.md`.
Prefer cheap models for extraction/verification volume
(`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `openai/gpt-6-luna`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`,
`claude-haiku-5-5-low` on devin which is ~$0.10/$0.50, free `swe-2-*`) and
reserve strong models for the synthesis call. Worker tier × N dominates —
orchestrator price barely matters. `--cache` memoizes identical calls
content-keyed across reruns; `batch()` on openrouter cuts ~40–60% for
latency-tolerant stages (one job, ≤24h window — poll defaults are
`batchPollMs`/`batchTimeoutMs` per call or in `agentflow.json`). The
research says: fan out on parallelizable
sub-questions, always end in centralized synthesis/verification
(independent agents amplify errors ~17×), and don't fan out sequential work.

**Guards:** the script body shadows `Date`, `Math` and `crypto` by default;
`Date.now()`, `new Date()`, `Math.random()` and `crypto.randomUUID()` throw a
clear error because nondeterminism silently misaligns `--resume`/`--cache`.
Use `--allow-nondeterminism` to pass the real globals (advisory — a script can
still reach `globalThis.Date`). `--max-agents <n>` (default 1000) caps total
`agent()` calls per run. `--retries <n>` (default 0) re-runs transient failures
— cheap models flake on empty completions under burst; `agent(p, {retries: 2})`
for volume stages. Never retried: `permissionDenied` and `timedOut`. All three
settable in `agentflow.json` (`"allowNondeterminism": true`, `"maxAgents": 200`,
`"retries": 1`).

**Backgrounded runs:** `--detach` returns immediately with a run-id (the child
keeps running, output in `.agentflow/runs/<id>.log`). `agentflow status <id>`
prints settled/total + outcome (exit 2 while running), `agentflow tail <id>`
streams journal events until run-end, and `agentflow watch [id]` renders a
live phase-grouped terminal view — each `phase()` becomes a group header
with done/total counts, lanes list underneath with status + elapsed, and
settled lanes show a one-line result summary (first sentence of the agent's
reply — the "what it found"). Declared `meta.phases` with no calls yet render
as upcoming; the footer carries token totals and counts, and run-end shows
the big-ASCII spend card. Falls back to `tail` output when piped. Add
`--tmux` alongside `--detach` to auto-open the watch pane beside your shell
(needs an active tmux session; the pane stays open on run-end for the spend
card). Use detach for long fan-outs and check back — same model as Claude's
detached Workflow.

## Autonomous operation

A launched run needs no babysitting — the runner owns the pool, retries,
SIGINT drain, and journaling. Your job is the loop around it:

1. **Launch** with `--detach` for anything longer than a few calls; keep the
   run-id it prints.
2. **Monitor** with `watch <id>` (TTY) or `status <id>` (scripts) — token
   totals accumulate per call on devin so spend is visible mid-run.
3. **Heal**: interrupted or partially failed runs resume exactly —
   `agentflow run w.mjs --resume <id> --harness <same>` replays settled
   work and re-runs only the gaps; mid-poll batch interrupts re-poll the
   journaled batch id, never resubmit. A `null` slot in results is a failed
   call — count it, retry the script with `--resume` if it matters, don't
   panic-rerun everything.
4. **Report** the synthesis + `run <id>` (journal keeps prompt/result text;
   `status`/`watch` keep totals).

Don't re-orchestrate per-call in your own context — that's the thing
agentflow exists to remove. If a stage needs a decision from you, gate it
between two `run` invocations, not inside the workflow.

`agentflow stop <id>` SIGTERMs the journaled pid only when it verifies as the
run's own process (agentflow cmdline + start time matching the journal — a
reused or unverifiable pid is never signaled), then waits for run-end up to
`grace + 15s`; a still-draining run stays resumable and `status` keeps
reporting it. Exit codes for `status`/`tail`: `0` ended ok, `1` ended
error/determinism-lint, `130` interrupted, `2` running / orphaned /
no-journal (stdout says which). A run whose pid is dead but journal has no
run-end reports **orphaned** — resume it with `agentflow run <script>
--resume <id>`; a re-run `run-start` supersedes the old `run-end`, so a
resumed run shows as running again.

All run commands are **cwd-rooted**: journals and worktrees resolve against
the run's `--cwd` (default: your shell cwd). Run `status`/`stop`/`clean` from
the same directory you ran `run` from (or pass `--cwd`).

`agentflow clean` reclaims worktrees of runs that are not live — including
orphaned ones — and runs `git worktree prune`. **`clean` force-removes**:
uncommitted agent work in a worktree is destroyed. Harvest or commit
anything you want from a worktree before cleaning; `--all` additionally
sweeps dirs under `.agentflow/worktrees/` with no journal record or live
registration.

## Safety

**A workflow script is arbitrary code that spawns credentialed agents.** Never
`agentflow run` a script you have not read — treat it like `curl | sh` with a
sandboxed subprocess per line. The runner inherits your harness credentials and
workspace permissions. Keep `.agentflow/` out of git (it is gitignored here;
journals contain prompt and result text).

## Authoring workflows (the point of the feature)

When a task fits "When to use", **you write the script** — the orchestration
plan is code you author, the runner just executes it. The workflow:

1. Decompose the task into independent units an agent can do in one session.
2. Decide phases: what runs in parallel, what waits, what verifies.
3. Choose models per stage — cheap model for extraction/verification volume,
   default/strong model only for synthesis or hard judgment.
4. Write the `.mjs` to scratch (`.agentflow/workflows/` or `/tmp`), show it to
   the user before running — the untrusted-script rule applies to scripts you
   write too.
5. Run it, report the synthesis, keep the journal's `run <id>` for resume.

Proven composition patterns (mirror Claude's own):

- **Classifier routing**: one agent classifies each item, routes to a
  specialized follow-up agent per class.
- **Fan-out + adversarial verify**: every researcher's finding gets a separate
  verifier agent before it reaches synthesis (see `workflows/deep-research.mjs`).
- **Compound loop**: plan -> work -> review -> compound as staged agents —
  `workflows/compound-loop.mjs` runs the compound-engineering loop; each
  stage is a fresh-context agent sharing cwd (needs the CE plugin installed).
- **Multi-angle drafting**: N agents draft the same plan/spec from different
  stated angles; a judge agent weighs them.
- **Map-reduce migration**: per-file transforms in parallel, then a sweep
  agent checks integration points the per-file view can't see.

## Minimal pattern

```js
export const meta = { name: 'audit', description: 'per-file review', phases: ['fan-out', 'synthesize'] };

phase('fan-out');
const reviews = await parallel(files.map(f => () =>
  agent(`Review ${f}`, { label: `rev:${f}`, model: 'claude-haiku-5-5-low' })
));

phase('synthesize');
const ok = reviews.filter(Boolean);      // nulls = failed agents, keep count
const summary = await agent(`Synthesize:\n${ok.map(r => r.text).join('\n')}`,
  { label: 'synthesis' });
log(summary?.text ?? 'synthesis failed');
```

See `examples/parallel-audit.mjs` for a complete script.

Write a multi-agent workflow once as a script, then run it on devin, claude, codex, opencode or hermes.

agentflow is a small Node runner. A workflow is an `.mjs` file; each `agent()` call spawns one non-interactive CLI session of the harness you pick, under a bounded concurrency pool, and every settled result is journaled so a run can be resumed. The plan lives in the script, not in a model's context window. This is the same idea as Claude Code's [dynamic workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows), delivered as a portable subprocess runner. ![agentflow social card: the mark, wordmark and an illustrative run ledger](assets/brand/social-card.png) > The image is a design proposal with illustrative log lines, not a capture. > TODO: replace with a real terminal recording of `agentflow tail` on a live run (needs paid or free-tier model calls, so it was not recorded here). ## Install Requires Node 20 or newer. ```bash npm install -g @lukedaduke/agentflow # or: npx @lukedaduke/agentflow agentflow doctor # which harness CLIs are on PATH ``` From a clone instead: ```bash git clone https://github.com/duketopceo/agentflow cd agentflow bin/agentflow doctor ``` ### As an agent plugin const results = await parallel(files.map((f) => () => agent(`Review ${f}`, { label: `review:${f}`, model: "cheap" }) )); const good = results.filter(Boolean); ``` Globals inside a script: `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`, `batch()`, `phase()`, `log()`, `args`. `batch()` fans out through the harness's async surface — one OR Batch job on `--harness openrouter` (~40–60% cheaper), one Devin Cloud session per item on `--harness devin` (`swe-2` models are free), one async sonar request per item on `--harness perplexity` (grounded, cited answers — the research surface), or first-party batch APIs on `--harness openai`/`--harness anthropic` (~50% off, 24h window). Results align to input order; resumable mid-poll. ## Watching a run `agentflow watch [run-id]` renders a live phase-grouped view from the run journal on an alternate screen — each `phase()` in the script becomes a group header with done/total counts, lanes list underneath with spinner/status/ elapsed, and settled lanes carry a one-line "what it found" result summary. Useful flags: `--harness`, `--concurrency`, `--via ori`, `--cache`, `--resume `, `--retries`, `--max-agents`, `--allow-nondeterminism`, `--detach`. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR S[workflow script .mjs] --> R[runtime: pool + journal] R -->|agent#40;#41; x N| P{adapter} P --> D[devin -p] P --> C[claude -p] P --> X[codex exec] P --> O[opencode run] P --> I[ori code] P --> H[openrouter HTTP] P -.->|--via ori| W[ori wraps the CLI] R --> J[(.agentflow/runs/id.jsonl)] J -->|--resume| R ``` - **Cross-harness** means: one script, and a thin adapter per CLI that builds argv, spawns the process, classifies failure (timeout, permission denial) and parses output into `{text, json}`. Sessions, tools and context are not shared; workers share only the filesystem. - **Journal:** each settled call is one line in `.agentflow/runs/.jsonl`. `--resume` replays settled calls by **content fingerprint** (prompt, model, schema, worktree, cwd, permission, via, reasoning effort), re-executing only calls whose spec changed or never finished. A settled *failure* replays as `null` — enough for a fallback chain to rotate to the next model — and a crashed call's dangling `in-flight` record is ignored, so crash recovery never needs journal surgery. Strip a settled record only to force re-execution of an unchanged spec. If the dead epoch's harness process is still running, `--resume` kills its process group first (`spawn` records in the journal carry the pgid). - **Limits you should know:** no sandbox beyond what each CLI enforces, no usage/cost numbers in the journal, schema output is parsed, validated against a JSON Schema subset, and repair-retried up to 5 times by default. ## Ops ```bash bin/agentflow run w.mjs --detach # background; journal keeps the record bin/agentflow status # progress; 'orphaned' if the pid died bin/agentflow stop # SIGTERM the journaled pid (resumable) bin/agentflow clean [--all] # reclaim worktrees of non-live runs (force!) node scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs # reproducible live-adapter matrix ``` Ops commands are cwd-rooted — run them from the directory you ran `run` from. `clean` force-removes worktrees (ended *and* orphaned runs): harvest agent work first. `agent(p, {worktree: 'auto'})` runs the call in its own `git worktree` under `.agentflow/worktrees/` — isolates file-mutating agents from the main checkout; `clean` reclaims them after the run ends. ## Docs - `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md` — agent-facing guidance (installed per harness) - `docs/plans/` — design history and the [program roadmap](docs/plans/2026-10-10-005-feat-program-roadmap-plan.md) - `docs/smoke-matrix.md` — live per-adapter verification results (`scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs` reproduces) - `docs/research/` — cross-harness landscape + orchestration economics; start with `2026-10-10-landscape.md` - `docs/publish-matrix.md` — per-harness distribution surfaces and publish paths - `docs/task-queue.md` — serializing expensive ops across parallel agents via `agent-task-queue` - `DESIGN.md` and `assets/brand/` — design direction and logo proposal ## Status Early development, v0.2. The mark is the product in one picture: **one input fans out to three parallel
agent branches that rejoin at one result.** Fan-out, then fan-in through the
script's synthesis step.

# agentflow design direction: "Run Ledger"

Status: proposal. Logo assets are in `assets/brand/` and need owner sign-off.

## Concept

agentflow's real interface is a **journal**: one JSONL line per settled agent
call, `[index] label -> ok | null`, read in a terminal. The direction takes
that literally: a **ledger** of small, tabular, monospaced entries on a cool,
quiet canvas, with one teal accent that means "this is the run's path". It is a
developer tool people watch for minutes, not a marketing site, so it is dense,
calm and numerically aligned.

## Research method and limits

The Refero MCP was not available in this session, so the `refero-design`
skill's style/screen/flow search could not run. Per its fallback, direction
comes from named references, the product's own output and the skill's bundled
craft rules. Treat the reference lock below as a hypothesis, to be checked
against Refero styles when the tool is available.

### Reference lock

- **Primary direction:** terminal-native ledger. The existing output of
  `agentflow tail` and the journal is the design source.
- **Preserve:** monospaced tabular columns for run data; one accent colour
  used only for the live path, the cursor and links; status carried by glyph
  plus word, never colour alone; dark canvas as the default in the terminal.
- **Borrow only:** Claude Code's `/workflows` phase list (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows)
  for phase-grouped progress; GitHub Actions-style one-line-per-step status rows
  for density.
- **Role rules:** teal is not a decorative gradient, not a button fill on the
  README, and not a success colour (success is green, see below).
- **Reject:** purple-to-blue "AI" gradients, robot or brain icons, glassy cards,
  swarm/constellation imagery, serif accent words.

### Decision ledger

| Decision | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Monospace for all run data | the journal and `tail` output | alignment of index, label, status, elapsed |
| Single teal accent | product concept: "the path through the run" | one meaning, easy to keep rare |
| Separate success green, failure red, pending amber | status semantics | accent must not double as status |
| Glyph plus word for every status | WCAG 1.4.1 (use of colour) | colour-blind safe; works in a monochrome terminal |
| Fork-join mark | architecture: fan-out, fan-in | the one thing the runner does |
| No motion in the CLI beyond a spinner | terminal norms | log output must stay greppable |

# Installing Agentflow for OpenCode

The plugin lives at `plugins/agentflow/` and ships **both** OpenCode plugin
contracts. The two OpenCode SDKs expose incompatible v2 plugin contexts, so the
two versions are **separate entrypoints** in one package — install whichever
matches your OpenCode.

| Your OpenCode | Entry | Install |
|---|---|---|
| **v1, `1.18.29+`** | `plugins/agentflow/v1.mjs` (`server()`) | `opencode plugin github:duketopceo/agentflow` |
| **v2 (`2.x`)** | `plugins/agentflow/v2.mjs` (`Plugin.define`) | `opencode plugin github:duketopceo/agentflow#main::path:plugins/agentflow` |

There is no `opencode plugin add` subcommand — the only verb is
`opencode plugin <module>`, and `add` is parsed as the module name.

The v1 entry requires `1.18.29` or newer (the release where object entrypoints
were added). On older v1 releases the `server` entry is not read.

Both entries expose the same two tools: `agentflow_run`, `agentflow_doctor`.

Requires Node.js >= 20 and `agentflow` on PATH (repo `bin/agentflow`, or
`npm link` inside the repo).

> **v2 status:** live-verified on the v2 beta build (`opencode-ai@beta`
> `0.0.0-beta-202608110357`, 2026-10-13) — `opencode plugin <repo>` installs,
> `debug agent build` lists both tools, and
> `debug agent build --tool agentflow_doctor --params '{}'` executes for real.
> On this build the default install resolves the `./server` entry — the `server()`
> contract still loads on v2; `./v2` (`Plugin.define`) remains for releases
> where `server()` is dropped.

## Reading a run's output

`agentflow run` writes its output — phase markers, per-lane results, and the
`[agentflow] run <id>` line — to **stderr**. Both entries capture stderr and
stdout together, so `agentflow_run` returns that text to you, including the
run-id you need to `status`, `stop`, or `--resume` the run.

If `agentflow` is not on `PATH`, the tool says so explicitly rather than
reporting a bare exit code; a timeout or oversized output is likewise named.

If you only want the agent-facing skill (it teaches opencode to shell out to
`agentflow run`), copy it:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config/opencode/skills/agentflow
cp /path/to/agentflow/skills/agentflow/SKILL.md ~/.config/opencode/skills/agentflow/SKILL.md
```

# Task queue — serializing expensive ops across parallel agents

Worker fan-out (`src/pool.mjs`, `agents/worker.md`) runs N agents in parallel.
Left alone, each invokes builds/tests/installs freely; on memory-tight boxes
compile + agents together trigger oomd kills (see the llama.cpp services in
the machine notes). `agent-task-queue`
([block/agent-task-queue](https://github.com/block/agent-task-queue), PyPI)
is the shared chokepoint: an MCP server with SQLite FIFO queues that
serializes the expensive parts.

## Install / registration

Launched per-harness as an MCP server — no daemon, no clone:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agent-task-queue": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["agent-task-queue@0.4.1"]
    }
  }
}
```

The version is **pinned** (`0.4.1`, exported as `TASK_QUEUE_VERSION` in
`src/taskqueue.mjs`); do not float `@latest` in registered config atoms. The
canonical atoms live in luke-agents (`scripts/mcp/` catalog) and the dotfiles
`.mcp.json` — the value multiplies when every harness (Claude, Cursor, Codex,
Devin) points at the same queue so non-agentflow sessions serialize too.

`agentflow doctor` prints a `note task-queue …` line reporting whether the
`uvx`/`uv` launcher is on PATH. It is informational only — the queue is
opt-in and never changes doctor's exit code.

## Queue topology

- `shared` — default queue for builds/tests. All workers on the machine
  serialize through it.
- `build/<worktree>` — leaf queues for stateful per-worktree work (configured
  via the server's `--queue-capacity` scopes when a shared parent cap is
  wanted). Unconfigured leaves are still independent FIFO queues.

`queue_name` is per `run_task` call, so workers opt in per command — no
global routing needed.

## Worker contract

Both worker prompts (`agents/worker.md`, `droids/worker.md`) carry the rule:
expensive commands (compilers, `npm test`, `cargo build`, `docker build`,
package installs) go through `run_task` on the `shared` queue when the tool
is available; `task_status(task_id, output_offset)` returns bounded
heartbeats mid-task instead of re-running. If the tool is absent the worker
runs the command directly — the queue must never become a hard dependency.

## Behaviour notes

- **FIFO**: strict ordering within each exact `queue_name`; queue wait time
  is unbounded (MCP holds the connection), `timeout_seconds` applies to
  execution only (default 1200s, hard auto-kill at 120min).
- **Zombie cleanup**: the server detects dead parents, kills orphaned
  children, and clears stale locks — a SIGKILLed worker leaves no orphaned
  `cargo build`.
- **Ephemeral state**: SQLite lives under `/tmp/agent-task-queue/` — queue
  state does not survive reboots. Acceptable; queues are ephemeral by nature.
- **Opt-in hole**: enforcement is cooperative. Permissive Bash rules let an
  agent bypass `run_task`; the sandboxing plan
  (`docs/plans/2026-10-19-003-eval-worker-sandboxing-plan.md`) is where
  mandatory enforcement would live.

---
name: worker
description: Cheap disposable worker for extraction, labeling, and single-file review inside agentflow workflows or ad-hoc fan-out.
model: inherit
tools:
  - read
  - grep
  - glob
  - exec
---

You are a single-purpose worker inside a fan-out. Do the named task on the
named files and return the requested format exactly — no exploration beyond
scope, no speculative fixes. When a `schema` or output contract is stated in
the prompt, respond with only the requested JSON.

Expensive commands — builds, test runs, heavy installs (compilers, `npm test`,
`cargo build`, `docker build`, package managers) — go through the
`agent-task-queue` MCP tool when it is available: call `run_task` with
`queue_name: "shared"` (or `"build/<worktree>"` for stateful per-worktree
work) instead of running the command directly. Sibling workers run
concurrently; the queue serializes the expensive parts so they don't thrash
the machine. Read progress with `task_status` rather than re-running. If the
tool is not available, run the command normally — never block on its
absence.

## 1. Symphony's completion contract, quoted precisely

The plan brief described Symphony's output as a "proof-of-work bundle (CI
status, PR review feedback, walkthrough videos)". That is the README/marketing
framing. The **spec itself defines completion more subtly — as a handoff
state plus reconciliation**, not a fixed artifact bundle:

- §1: *"A successful run can end at a workflow-defined handoff state (for
  example `Human Review`), not necessarily `Done`."*
- §11.5: *"Workflow-specific success often means 'reached the next handoff
  state' (for example `Human Review`) rather than tracker terminal state
  `Done`."*
- §7.1: *"A successful worker exit does not mean the issue is done forever."*

Mechanically the spec separates three things agentflow currently conflates
into "settled":

1. **Worker exit** (the agent process finished, normally or not),
2. **Workflow-defined success** (the issue reached a declared handoff state —
   judged by re-reading the tracker, not by the exit code), and
3. **Evidence location** — the proof artifacts (PR, CI status, comments) are
   written by *the coding agent itself* via provider-native tools: §11.5,
   *"Ticket mutations (state transitions, comments, attachments, PR metadata)
   are typically handled by the coding agent through the selected adapter's
   provider-native tools."* The orchestrator never sees or validates the
   proof; it re-reads the work source.

So "proof-of-work" in the spec = *the work source says the handoff happened*,
re-verified by the orchestrator on every poll tick (§8.5 reconciliation stops
runs whose issue left an active state). There is no proof schema; there is a
re-check loop.

## 2. AX manifest model, condensed

`ax.io/v1alpha1`, four kinds, multi-doc YAML:

- **Task** — smallest unit of isolated execution. `spec.image` must be
  digest-pinned (*"a tag can move and would silently invalidate the actor's
  snapshots"*), `resources.limits` only (no requests), at most one `Workspace`
  binding, `spec.config` = arbitrary ≤16 KiB YAML handed to the runner
  verbatim, whole spec immutable once created. `spec.debug: true` is the
  opt-in that makes `ax ssh` work.
- **Workspace** — declarative environment materialized once, bindable by many
  tasks: git repos cloned at revision, literal `files`, MCP
  registries/servers, skill registries + materialization path.
- **Model** — provider + model id + parameters + `secretKey` reference, as a
  cluster resource so rotation/pinning is one `ax apply`.
- **Lifecycle** — `ax suspend` / `ax resume` = *"checkpoint actor state and
  pause"* / *"pick up where it left off"* (Substrate actor snapshots; this is
  why images must be digest-pinned). `status.phase` + conditions
  (`WorkspaceReady`, `Ready`/`Suspended`). `ax ssh` for live inspection.
- AX explicitly refuses to model agent fan-out: *"An agent is not one process
  that runs to completion... AX does not try to model that shape"* — the Task
  is the tree node, the agent composes them.

## 3. Primitive diff and verdicts

| Primitive | Symphony | AX | agentflow today | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Work source | board poll (Linear) + reconciliation | manifest apply | workflow script invoked by user/agent; journal + Hey posts | **Reject** polling; **note** claim state machine |
| Unit | isolated per-issue workspace + worker turns | immutable Task actor | settled `agent()` call in a run; `worktree:'auto'` | **Adapt** — hooks, not actors |
| Completion | handoff state re-verified against tracker | task `status.phase`/conditions | settled journal line (exit/result only) | **Adopt** — declared completion evidence |
| Environment | `WORKFLOW.md` hooks (`after_create`/`before_run`/`after_run`/`before_remove`) | Workspace manifest (git+files+MCP+skills) | `worktree:'auto'` checkout, no setup hooks | **Adapt** — run-scoped setup hooks |
| Model config | `codex.*` config in WORKFLOW.md | `Model` resource + `secretKey` | `--model`/`--via` flags + keyring | **Reject** — already covered |
| Supervision | none — spec: manage work, not agents | `watch`/`ssh`/`suspend`/`resume` | `tail`/`watch`/`status`/`stop`, journal-replay resume | **Reject** ssh/suspend; keep replay-resume |
| Release model | spec-first, impl optional | CRDs + controller | journal format implicit in code | **Adapt** — version the journal schema |

### Rationale per row

**Work source — reject the poll loop, keep the state machine in the pocket.**
Symphony's Unclaimed→Claimed→Running→RetryQueued→Released machine (§7.1)
exists to dedupe dispatches against a mutable external board. agentflow has no
board; a run starts because someone exec'd it. If a Kurultai-Hey-style board
integration ever lands, this is the right model to copy — file it, don't
build it.

**Unit — adapt.** AX's immutable-Task-actor is fleet machinery. But
Symphony's insight that a unit of work deserves *lifecycle hooks around a
persistent workspace* maps directly onto `worktree:'auto'`, which today
provisions `.agentflow/worktrees/<name>` and nothing else. A `before_run`
hook (install deps, materialize fixtures) is the piece both systems
independently arrived at and we lack.

**Completion — adopt.** This is the load-bearing finding, detailed in §4.

**Environment — adapt.** AX's `Workspace` manifest is a per-worktree
environment spec. agentflow's workflow `.mjs` already *is* a repo-owned
executable contract (Symphony's `WORKFLOW.md` with `meta` front matter, but
Turing-complete). The missing delta is declarative setup, not a new manifest
format: hooks, or at most a `workspace` option on `agent()` that names a
provision script.

**Model — reject.** `Model` as a resource solves rotation across a fleet;
agentflow's `model`/`via` per-call options plus keyring cover it on one box.

**Supervision — reject, with the interesting nuance.** `ax suspend/resume`
is process checkpointing — real value on a fleet where a suspended sandbox
frees a VM. On one laptop, a suspended worker frees ~nothing (memory
pressure is the only win, and `SIGSTOP` exists). agentflow's journal-replay
`--resume` is the *better* single-box primitive: deterministic, cheap,
survives reboots, and U3's stale-result guard makes it safe. Borrow nothing
here except the vocabulary (`Suspended` as a phase name if runs ever get
phases).

**Release model — adapt.** Symphony shipped SPEC.md as the product with an
optional reference impl. agentflow's journal is already a de-facto spec
(`src/journal.mjs` documents record types in comments) consumed by `tail`,
`watch`, `status`, `--resume`. It deserves a `type: 'run-start'` schema
version field so external consumers can feature-detect — cheap insurance
before the journal grows proof records (below).

## 4. If we borrow one thing

**Declared completion evidence on the settled record.** Today a run is "done"
when the last `agent()` call settles and `run-end` is appended — the journal
records *that* the process exited, nothing about whether the work landed.
Symphony's actual mechanism (re-check the work source) doesn't port — our
work source is the caller — but its *contract shape* does: let a workflow
declare what counts as done, and let the runner evaluate and journal it.

Concrete change candidate, smallest version: `agent()` accepts
`proof: { tests?, diff?, command? }` — after settle, the runner evaluates the
declared check (e.g. `command` exits 0, `diff` non-empty in the worktree) and
records the outcome on the settled line and aggregates into `run-end`. A run
then reports `ok` vs `ok-unproven` instead of conflating exit status with
task status. This is exactly Symphony's *"successful worker exit does not
mean the issue is done"* enforced at the point agentflow can actually see.

Secondary candidates (named, not committed):

1. `before_run`/`after_run` hooks for `worktree:'auto'` workspaces (Symphony
   §9.4 / AX Workspace, lite).
2. A `journal` schema version field in `run-start` (Symphony's spec-first
   release pattern, applied to our one real interface per DESIGN.md).
3. A `Suspended`-style phase vocabulary if/when U12 (terminal progress view)
   lands — vocabulary only, no checkpointing.

## 5. Non-goals confirmed

- No K8s/Substrate/actor runtimes — laptop tool.
- No board poller/daemon — revisit only if Hey-board dispatch becomes real.
- No `ssh`-into-worker or process checkpoint — `tail`/`watch` and
  journal-replay resume already win on one box.

# Decision: policy interception (`govern()`) in the worker path

**Status:** decided — **adopt the pattern, not the toolkit** (thin governor, no SDK dependency)
**Date:** 2026-11-01
**Plan:** `docs/plans/2026-10-19-004-eval-policy-interception-govern-plan.md`
**Sibling:** `docs/plans/2026-10-19-003-eval-worker-sandboxing-plan.md`
**Evidence:** `evals/policy-interception/` (scratch harness, 13/13 scenarios green)

## Verdict

Adopt the **pattern** — a thin `govern()`-style wrapper plus hash-chained audit —
without taking `@microsoft/agent-governance-sdk` as a runtime dependency.

## What was evaluated

Microsoft's `agent-governance-toolkit` (6.4k★, MIT). Its headline `govern(fn,
policy)` API is Python-first; the TypeScript SDK
(`@microsoft/agent-governance-sdk@5.0.0`, "public preview — APIs may change")
installs cleanly on Node ≥20 (verified on v26.7.0, aarch64) and provides
`PolicyEngine`, `AuditLogger`, `AgentMeshClient`, plus identity/trust/rings.

The scratch harness wraps a representative worker tool surface (`shell.exec`,
`fs.write`, `net.fetch`) with a YAML policy: deny destructive shell, deny egress
off an allowlist, `require_approval` on writes outside the worktree,
fail-closed default. All 13 scenarios pass: allow executes, deny raises
`GovernanceDenied` with no partial execution, `require_approval` parks the call
and resumes on grant (or clears on reject), the audit trail records decision +
inputs per call, and tampering with an exported log is caught by re-verifying
the SHA-256 hash chain.

## Why the SDK isn't the dependency

1. **agentflow's tool surface isn't where the SDK aims.** `govern()` wraps
   in-process function calls. agentflow's workers are *external CLI processes*
   spawned through `spawnProcess` (`src/adapters/base.mjs:8`) /
   `spawnAgent` (`src/adapters/base.mjs:238`). The tool calls that matter —
   what `claude`, `devin`, `codex` do inside their own runtimes — are
   invisible to a wrapper in our process no matter which library provides it.
   The honest interception point in agentflow is the **spawn boundary**:
   argv construction, binary allowlist, cwd, env. Governing that needs ~100
   lines, not a 60-export SDK.
2. **The condition language can't express our rules.** `evaluatePolicy`
   supports `==`, `!=`, numeric comparison, `in`/`not in`, boolean flags,
   `and`/`or` — **no substring, glob, or regex on values**. "Deny `rm -rf`"
   and "non-allowlisted host" can't live in the YAML; the harness precomputes
   `destructive`, `host_allowed`, `outside_worktree` in JS and passes them as
   booleans. The real policy logic already lives in our wrapper — the SDK
   contributes dispatch and a verdict enum.
3. **Audit is in-memory only.** `AuditLogger` is a well-built hash chain
   (each entry's hash covers content + previous hash; `getEntries` returns
   defensive copies; eviction keeps a seam hash) but has **no import/load** —
   `exportJSON` only. Restart persistence and post-hoc verification must be
   bolted on anyway (the harness does it in ~30 lines, `verifyAuditFile`).
   Inputs ride in `skillAuditMetadata` — undocumented, discovered from source.
4. **Maturity.** Public preview, APIs may change; the legacy `evaluate()` path
   returns `require_approval` at runtime but types it as `'review'`. For a
   security-critical seam, that's the wrong direction of stability leverage.

## What the pattern buys us

A `govern()`-equivalent around `spawnProcess`/`spawnAgent` gives agentflow:
per-invocation policy (binary allowlist, forbidden-flag rules, worktree
confinement checks), an approval gate seam for human-in-the-loop runs, and a
tamper-evident decision log next to the existing journal (`src/journal.mjs`).
If a follow-on wants the SDK's real differentiators — Ed25519 agent identity,
trust scoring, OPA/Cedar backends, the Claude Code plugin — it's an additive
upgrade behind the same seam, not a prerequisite.

## Layering contract (reconciling with the sandboxing plan)

> **govern = intent policy, sandbox = capability boundary.**

govern() decides whether an action *should* run (per call, with approvals and
an audit trail). Sandboxing decides what the process *can* do (fs/net
restrictions enforced below the JS layer). Neither substitutes for the other:

- **Blind spot of govern() (verified in harness, scenario 9):** an unwrapped
  code path executes unaudited — a worker that spawns around the wrapper
  defeats it entirely. Intent policy must therefore sit at the single choke
  point (`spawnProcess`) AND be paired with process-level isolation.
- **Blind spot of sandboxing:** it can't express "ask a human first" or
  record intent — a capability boundary has no approval concept.

## Follow-on (separate work)

- Wrap `spawnProcess` (`src/adapters/base.mjs`) with a local governor:
  action = `worker.spawn`, context = `{bin, argv, cwd, adapter}`; deny rules
  for binary allowlist violations and `--dangerously-*`-class flags;
  audit entries appended to the journal as hash-chained records.
- Approval UX: none exists in-process today; a `require_approval` verdict can
  surface as a queued prompt in `watch`/`cli` before resume.
- Re-evaluate the SDK if/when MCP-level governance (ContextForge) or
  per-agent identity lands — that's where its identity/trust modules earn
  their weight.

## Honest notes

- Python SDK is the mature surface (`govern(fn)` decorator, richer condition
  handling); running a Python sidecar for a Node codebase to wrap spawn calls
  is not justified — the TS parity gap is a point against the lib, not the
  pattern.
- Everything audited is advisory until the wrap lands at the single spawn
  choke point. Any new direct `spawn`/`execFile` call site is a policy bypass.
- Test scenario caveat: the harness's `destructive` regex is illustrative,
  not a production classifier; shell-command classification belongs in the
  follow-on and needs its own test corpus.

# Decision: worker sandboxing

**Status:** decided · **Date:** 2026-11-01 · **Plan:** `docs/plans/2026-10-19-003-eval-worker-sandboxing-plan.md`

## TL;DR

**Adopt `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` (`srt`) as the worker boundary now; defer OpenShell; keep smokescreen in reserve for shared/per-client egress policy.** All three candidates were verified on this box (aarch64, Asahi kernel 7.2.x); the choice is driven by weight and threat model, not feasibility.

## Threat model — what this defends against

Answer to the plan's framing question: **both, weighted toward (a).**

- **(a) Buggy/hallucinated destructive commands** — the common case. Covered by `srt`'s filesystem boundary (verified: writes outside `allowWrite` fail EROFS).
- **(b) Prompt-injected workers doing exfiltration** — partially covered today by `srt`'s network allowlist (verified: non-allowlisted domains blocked at the proxy with `X-Proxy-Error: blocked-by-allowlist`). Full (b) coverage — blocking IP-literal exfil, per-worker egress identity, SSRF-grade range rules — is smokescreen's territory and is deferred below.
- **Credentials** — `srt` does not address ambient credential visibility (agents still see real tokens). That stays at the MCP/oauth-broker layer; see *Layer ownership*.

## Evaluation evidence (aarch64 / Asahi, `omarchy-max`, 2026-11-01)

### sandbox-runtime (`@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime@0.0.81`, `srt` CLI)

- **Install:** `npm install` clean; Linux deps `bwrap` + `socat` already present on the host.
- **Inside-boundary normal op:** `srt -c 'echo hello > work/out.txt && node -e …'` → wrote file, ran node (`arm64`), exit 0. No functionality loss.
- **Denied write:** `echo x > outside/esc.txt` → `Read-only file system`, `WRITE_RC=1`. Enforced via bubblewrap mount namespace.
- **Denied egress:** `curl https://evil.example/` → `X-Proxy-Error: blocked-by-allowlist`, `CURL_RC=7`. Network namespace removed entirely; traffic routes through unix-socket proxies on the host.
- **Allowed egress:** `curl https://example.com/` (allowlisted) → `200`.
- **Overhead:** ~120–230 ms per spawn (bwrap setup + proxy spawn), near-zero steady-state CPU delta (`user 0.354s` sandboxed vs `0.370s` bare for identical workload). For workers that run minutes, overhead is far under the 10% gate; for per-command wrapping it is a fixed ~0.1–0.2 s tax.

### OpenShell (NVIDIA, v0.1.6 docs + host prerequisites)

- **Support matrix:** aarch64 Linux is *listed supported* — static-musl CLI, `linux/arm64` images for both cluster and gateway containers.
- **Host prereqs verified:** Docker Engine 29.9.2 (needs ≥28.0) ✓; `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK=y` and `landlock` in `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` ✓; seccomp standard ✓. Podman absent (docker driver would be used).
- **Not installed.** The gate passes on paper, but even the minimal path is a systemd-user gateway service + control plane + per-sandbox containers — disproportionate to the current need. Telemetry is anonymous-on with env opt-out.
- **Distinctive value** (credential injection at the gateway, seccomp+Landlock syscall layer, declarative policy with formal diff-proving) doesn't match today's primary threat (a).

### smokescreen (stripe, v0.1.0)

- **Build:** `go install github.com/stripe/smokescreen@latest` → clean aarch64 binary, `smokescreen --help` works.
- **Live ACL test:** ran on `127.0.0.1:4750` with a `default` service ACL (`allowed_domains: [example.com]`, `allow_missing_role`):
  - `http://example.com/` via proxy → `200` ✓
  - `http://evil.example/` → `407` deny ✓
  - `http://169.254.169.254/` (metadata IP) → `407` deny ✓ — the SSRF-grade IP blocking `srt`'s domain allowlist doesn't do.
- **Caveats found:** role extraction defaults to TLS client-cert CN — per-client ACLs mean running mTLS, which is real machinery for a local tool. `allow_missing_role` + a `default:` ACL block is the low-effort mode.

## Comparison matrix

| | sandbox-runtime | OpenShell | smokescreen |
|---|---|---|---|
| aarch64 verified | **yes, live** (fs+net denies enforced) | docs-supported + host prereqs verified; not installed | **yes, live** (allow/deny/SSRF blocks) |
| Boundary | userspace: bwrap fs + proxy net | kernel: Landlock+seccomp + gateway | egress-only CONNECT proxy |
| Weight | wrap a command (`srt -c`) | control plane (gateway svc + containers) | one Go binary + ACL file |
| Credentials | ambient | injected at gateway | doesn't see creds |
| IP-literal/SSRF blocking | no (domains only) | yes (policy) | **yes (verified)** |
| Per-client egress identity | no | yes | yes, via mTLS CN (heavier) |
| Telemetry | none | anonymous, opt-out env | none |
| Overhead measured | ~0.12–0.23 s/spawn, ~0% CPU | — | proxy hop only |

## Decision

1. **Now — sandbox-runtime wraps worker spawns.** Wrap point: `applyVia()` in `src/adapters/base.mjs` — the same mechanism that already prefixes `ori`; `srt --settings <file>` becomes a composable `via` prefix. Per-worktree `allowWrite` (the spawn `cwd` is already the worker's isolated worktree — `src/runtime.mjs` creates one per task) plus a workflow-declared `allowedDomains` list. This lands as follow-on implementation work; the decision is which boundary, not the patch.
2. **Deferred — smokescreen**, for when we need what `srt`'s net layer lacks: IP-literal/CIDR egress rules, a single shared ACL file across N concurrent workers, or per-worker egress identity. Trigger: first workflow whose workers talk to a dynamic set of hosts, or first exfiltration-oriented eval finding.
3. **Deferred — OpenShell**, revisited when workers must hold real credentials (its gateway injection removes ambient tokens entirely) or when a fleet/control-plane need exists. Re-check then on aarch64 + docker-driver status.

## Layer ownership (vs. ContextForge / mcp-oauth-broker)

- **fs + process egress:** `srt` at the adapter spawn layer.
- **MCP credential brokering:** the oauth-broker/ContextForge plan owns raw-token custody for MCP tools. `srt` narrows *where* a stolen token can be *sent* (allowlist); the broker narrows whether the worker *has* it. Complementary, not overlapping.
- **OpenShell's credential injection** would partially subsume the broker's job — if it ever lands, the decision doc for that migration must say which layer owns token custody.

## Honest limitations

- **This protects agent-spawned processes, not the user.** Anything a user runs outside the boundary is unrestricted — by design.
- `srt` userspace boundary ≠ kernel LSM: a worker that can `bwrap`/unshare creatively or exploit a setuid path is out of scope; that's OpenShell's seccomp layer, deferred with it.
- `srt` network filtering is domain-based; `curl 1.2.3.4` to an exfil IP bypasses the domain allowlist unless proxies reject literals — noted as a smokescreen trigger, not silently ignored.
- OpenShell aarch64 support is docs-verified, not boot-verified; a future re-evaluation should smoke `openshell` on this box before committing.

# Agentflow: Cross-Harness Dynamic Workflows - Plan

## Goal Capsule

- **Objective:** An agent running in Devin CLI (and equally in OpenCode, Claude Code, or Codex) can turn a large task into a saved, rerunnable orchestration script that fans out dozens of parallel subagent sessions, holds intermediate results in script variables, and returns only a final answer to the orchestrator's context — matching the capability shape of Claude Code's dynamic workflows.
- **Means:** a zero-dependency Node.js CLI (`agentflow`) that executes a JavaScript workflow script with injected globals (`agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`, `phase()`, `log()`), each `agent()` call spawning a one-shot harness CLI session as a subprocess; distributed from one repo as a multi-manifest plugin with a per-harness skill (KTD1, KTD2, KTD5).
- **Authority hierarchy:** this plan → `~/bin/gh-new-repo` conventions → Devin CLI docs (permissions, subagents, plugins) → each harness's `--help` surface.
- **Execution profile:** normal code path — branch, tests, PR.
- **Stop conditions:** a named harness CLI cannot run non-interactively with tool approval handled (plan's feasibility premise fails); unit tests cannot pass without real-model calls.
- **Who finishes:** `ce-work` implements; `lfg` pipeline ships to PR.

---

## Product Contract

### Summary

Build `agentflow`, a small standalone runner that mirrors Claude Code's dynamic-workflows feature for harnesses that lack it. An orchestrating agent writes a JS script; the runner executes it with a concurrency pool, spawning one-shot CLI agent sessions as subprocesses and returning structured results into script variables. The repo ships per-harness skills that teach each agent when to reach for it and how to write the scripts, packaged so `devin plugins install`, Claude's plugin loader, Codex, and OpenCode can each pick it up from the same repository.

### Problem Frame

Claude Code's dynamic workflows moved orchestration into code: a script holds the loop, the branching, and intermediate state, while a runtime pools tens-to-hundreds of subagents. Devin, Codex, and OpenCode can each fan out subagents, but only turn-by-turn through the orchestrating model's context — which caps parallelism, loses rerunnability, and puts every intermediate result on the orchestrator's token bill. On this machine all four CLIs are installed (`devin` 3000.11.3, `claude` 2.1.292, `codex` 0.160.1, `opencode` 1.18.33), and each has a documented non-interactive mode, so the substrate exists; what is missing is the executor and the shared script contract.

### Requirements

**Runner core**

- R1. `agentflow run <script.mjs>` executes a workflow script with top-level `await`, exposing `agent()`, `parallel()`, `pipeline()`, `phase()`, `log()`, and an `args` global.
- R2. Each `agent()` call spawns one one-shot session of the configured harness CLI as a subprocess and resolves to that agent's final result, or `null` on unrecoverable failure — matching Claude's `agent()` semantics.
- R3. Agent calls run under a bounded concurrency pool (default 8, configurable via flag and `agentflow.json`), with calls beyond the limit queued.
- R4. `agent()` options accepted per call: `{ label, model, schema, worktree, cwd, timeout }`; unknown options warn rather than fail.
- R5. A journal at `.agentflow/runs/<run-id>.jsonl` records every settled `agent()` call; `agentflow run --resume <run-id>` replays settled results and re-executes unsettled ones. On interrupt (SIGINT/SIGTERM), the runner stops dequeuing new calls, lets in-flight agents finish or kills them after a grace period, journals settled results, and exits leaving the run resumable.
- R6. When `schema` is passed, the runner returns parsed JSON for that agent: native structured-output flags where the harness has them, prompt-level instruction plus JSON extraction where it does not, `null` when parsing fails.

**Harness adapters**

- R7. One adapter per harness — `devin`, `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` — mapping the generic spawn spec to that CLI's flags per the capability matrix in Sources & Research, plus an `echo` adapter that returns a canned response for tests.
- R8. Harness selection is per-run (`--harness` flag, config default `devin`); a script may not mix harnesses in v1.
- R9. Each adapter defaults to that harness's least-privileged unattended mode (per KTD7); escalation is an explicit per-call or per-run option.
- R10. `agentflow doctor` reports which harness CLIs are on PATH and verifies the flags the adapter relies on exist (`--version`/help probes), exiting non-zero on failure.

**Distribution**

- R11. The repo installs as a plugin in each target harness: Agent Plugins root `plugin.json` + `.devin-plugin/` for Devin, `.claude-plugin/` for Claude, `.codex-plugin/` for Codex, `.opencode/` for OpenCode.
- R12. A `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md` teaches every harness the trigger conditions (fan-out beyond a handful of agents, codified rerunnable orchestration, adversarial/verification passes), the script API, cost guidance, and how to run/resume.
- R13. `examples/` contains runnable workflow scripts (parallel audit, multi-angle research) that run against the `echo` adapter with no model spend.

### Scope Boundaries

- **Out of scope (v1):** mixing harnesses inside one script; a TUI/dashboard for watching runs; `devin --cloud` sessions as agents; an OpenCode-native custom tool registration; editing any harness's internals.
- **Deferred to follow-up work:** CE-converter pipeline for emitting per-harness formats mechanically; OpenCode plugin-registered `workflow` tool; `devin --cloud` adapter variant; npm/binary distribution beyond the repo checkout.

### Key Decisions

- **Cross-harness plugin in its own repo** (session-settled: user-directed — chosen over config inside an existing repo: user asked for portability across Devin, OpenCode, Claude, Codex). Governs R11, R12.
- **All four harnesses in v1** (session-settled: user-directed — chosen over Devin-only: user named the harness set). Governs R7, R8.
- **Feasibility is settled, not probed** (session-settled: user-directed — user conditioned the project on "if that's possible"; every named harness's non-interactive surface was verified this session — see Sources & Research). Governs the project existing at all.

### Success Criteria

- `agentflow run examples/parallel-audit.mjs --harness echo` completes a multi-agent script locally with zero model spend.
- A real `devin -p`-backed workflow completes end-to-end on this machine (manual smoke — costs tokens, run once).
- `devin plugins install --local <repo>` exposes `/agentflow:*` skills; `claude`, `codex`, and `opencode` each see the skill/agent surface through their own plugin formats.

### Actors

- A1. **Orchestrating agent** — a Devin/Claude/Codex/OpenCode session that writes and launches the script; holds only the final result.
- A2. **Workflow agent** — a spawned one-shot CLI session; sees only its prompt, works in the given `cwd`/worktree.
- A3. **Operator** — the human who installs the plugin, runs `doctor`, picks models, and reads reports.

---

## Planning Contract

### Key Technical Decisions

- KTD1. **Subprocess fan-out is the execution model.** Each `agent()` spawns a one-shot harness CLI (`devin -p`, `claude -p`, `codex exec`, `opencode run`) rather than calling an SDK or API. This is the only mechanism that works identically across all four harnesses today, gives each agent a genuinely clean context, and inherits the harness's own auth, sandboxing, and permission model. Rejected alternatives: in-process subagent pools (no such API exists outside Claude), harness-specific SDKs (four integrations to maintain, uneven coverage), a skill that only teaches ad-hoc scripting (no rerunnable, journaled, verified artifact).
- KTD2. **Mirror Claude's workflow script API.** Globals: `agent(prompt, opts)`, `parallel(tasks)`, `pipeline(items, fn)`, `phase(name)`, `log(msg)`, `args`, and `export const meta = { name, description }`. Same names, same `null`-on-failure contract, so scripts port between Claude Code and agentflow with minimal edits. Rejected: inventing a divergent API (loses the main benefit — familiarity and portability of scripts Claude can already write).
- KTD3. **Zero-dependency Node.js, single CLI entry.** Plain `node` ESM, no npm packages: `bin/agentflow` → `src/*.mjs`. Node is present wherever these harnesses run; the workflow scripts are JavaScript by definition (KTD2), so a JS host avoids an embedded engine. Rejected: Python (would need a JS engine to host the scripts), Bun (not universally installed; CE-plugin parity is nice-to-have, not load-bearing).
- KTD4. **Adapter contract: `spawnAgent(spec) → Promise<{text, json?, exitCode, stderrTail}>`.** Spec fields map to the per-harness matrix below; each adapter owns flag mapping and output parsing (stdout text; harness-native JSON where available — `codex --output-schema`, `claude --json-schema`, `opencode --format json`; Devin falls back to prompt-instructed JSON extraction).
- KTD5. **One repo, multi-manifest packaging.** Root `plugin.json` (Agent Plugins 1.0.0 — Devin loads this spec natively), plus `.devin-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.opencode/` following the compound-engineering repo's proven layout. No converter build step in v1 — the per-harness manifests are thin enough to author directly. Rejected: depending on the CE converter CLI (extra build tooling for four small JSON files).
- KTD6. **Journal-based resume.** Append-only JSONL per run keyed by call sequence index; `--resume` returns journaled results without respawning. Deterministic replay is a script-authoring discipline (documented: avoid `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in call ordering — same constraint Claude imposes), not enforced by the runtime in v1.
- KTD7. **Least-privilege default per harness.** Devin: `--permission-mode smart` (auto-approves judged-safe, prompts never reach a headless run — denial is surfaced as failure); Codex: `-s workspace-write`; OpenCode: no `--auto` unless the script author sets it; Claude: `--allowedTools` restricted to read-only set by default. Escalation (`--permission-mode dangerous`, `danger-full-access`, `--auto`, broad tools) is an explicit `agent()` or run-level option the operator opts into.
- KTD8. **The skill is the trigger, the runner is the engine.** Capabilities (pooling, journaling, schema extraction, worktrees) live in `agentflow`; the SKILL.md carries the judgment — when fan-out beats `run_subagent`-style delegation, how to write the script, cost guidance (cheap models for mechanical extraction, expensive for judgment — matching the user's spend ceiling). **Goal:** `agentflow run script.mjs` executes a JS workflow with the injected global contract.

**Approach:** inject globals by wrapping the script source in an async function context (`AsyncFunction` or `node:vm`) — no bundler needed. Because `export` is illegal inside a wrapped body, the runtime first statically extracts the `export const meta = {...}` literal (the same plain-object-literal constraint Claude documents) and strips it from the evaluated source, using `meta` for `list`/resume display. `agent()` enqueues onto the pool, calls the resolved adapter, returns `{text, json}` or `null`. `parallel()`/`pipeline()` are thin helpers over `Promise.all` with per-item `null` preservation (mirroring documented Claude semantics). Journal index = monotonic call counter per run; resume compares call sequence. Progress output — the no-TUI equivalent of Claude's `/workflows` view — is a human-readable stderr stream: `phase()`/`log()` lines plus one line per agent settle (`label`, ok/null, elapsed, model). Interrupt behavior per R5.

**Test scenarios:**

- Happy path: script calling `agent()` 5× via `echo` adapter completes; results array in order.
- Concurrency: 10 calls, `--concurrency 3` → max 3 in-flight at any moment (assert via fake-adapter delay + counter).
- `parallel()` preserves `null` slots when two of five agents fail.
- Journal: kill mid-run, `--resume` replays settled calls without respawning (assert adapter invocation count unchanged for settled indices).
- Interrupt: SIGINT mid-run with queued-but-unstarted calls → unsettled calls never spawn, journal holds settled results, `--resume` completes the run.
- Error path: script syntax error → clean failure message naming the script, non-zero exit.

# Agentflow v0.2 — fused cross-harness plugin, verified adapters, distribution

## Problem Frame

v0.1 (PR #1, open) delivers the runner + 7 adapters + per-harness plugin
surfaces, but four adapters have never executed a real session, the Claude
parity gaps are unaddressed, the "one install pulls the whole stack" claim
is only half-wired (`optionalPlugins` doesn't auto-install), and there is no
real distribution story (no marketplace manifests, private repo blocks
anonymous plugin installs). v0.2 turns the working prototype into the fused
plugin the user described: dynamic workflows + the compound-engineering skill
suite installable in one step per harness, verified against live sessions at
the cheapest feasible cost posture.

## Scope

### In scope

- Merge/land PR #1 as precondition (user action — merge is not agent-granted).
- Live-smoke every adapter; record results in the adapter matrix.
- Cheap-first test posture: devin `swe-2-*` (free tier), opencode free models,
  ori/openrouter on `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`-class slugs. Avoid claude-native and
  codex-native subscription burn — codex smoke runs `--via ori` instead.
- cube-sandbox (`localhost:3000`, key `omaseal: cubesandbox/api-key`) as the
  isolation target for the escalated-permission smoke cases.
- Fidelity gaps worth closing now: determinism lint, run-level agent cap,
  README/workflow documentation of what was deferred.
- CE fusion: devin `requiredPlugins` upgrade + a shipped `compound-loop`
  workflow expressing plan→work→review→compound as executable phases.
- opencode native plugin file (`.opencode/plugins/agentflow.ts`).
- Distribution: claude/codex marketplace manifests so
  `claude plugin marketplace add duketopceo/agentflow` and
  `codex plugin marketplace add duketopceo/agentflow` work; README install
  matrix; repo visibility decision carried to the user.

### Out of scope

- Hosted/daemon services, harness internals, the Linear-tool idea.
- True OR batch API adapter (`:batch` is a separate async API — research
  doc §3; backlog item).
- `--detach`/background mode and worktree-pool isolation (documented as
  backlog; agents can background the CLI themselves today).
- npm publishing (deferred until name/tag settled).

- **R1.** PR #1 merged to `main` before v0.2 branches — *precondition requiring user action*.
- **R2.** Every non-echo adapter executes ≥1 real headless call and the result is recorded in `docs/research/cross-harness-dynamic-workflows.md` §3.

## Problem

Cheap models flake: the e2e deep-research run saw 5/12 `openrouter: empty
completion` failures under burst concurrency. Each null means a dropped
researcher/verifier — graceful but lossy. A bounded retry converts most flakes
into slightly slower successes.

## Scope

- `retries` spec opt on `agent()` + run-level default `--retries <n>` and
  `agentflow.json` `"retries"`. Default 0 (off) — opt-in, since retries
  multiply worst-case spend.
- Retry on `ok:false` EXCEPT `permissionDenied` (won't heal) and `timedOut`
  (rerun just burns another timeout). Linear backoff: `1000ms * attempt`.
- Log attempts via existing logLine; journal only the terminal settle
  (existing journal/resume semantics unchanged — a retried-then-ok call is one
  settled result at its call index; cache keys unchanged).
- Not in scope: backoff jitter config, per-error-type policy, circuit breakers.

## Implementation

- `src/runtime.mjs`: `retries` into KNOWN_AGENT_OPTS; resolve per call as
  `spec.retries ?? opts.retries ?? 0`; wrap the spawn call in a bounded loop,
  `logLine(\`${label} retry ${k}/${retries}\`)` between attempts, sleep
  `1000*k`.
- `src/cli.mjs`: `--retries` flag + `config.retries`.
- `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`: one line under Cost discipline/Guards.

## Tests

- `tests/runtime.test.mjs`: echo adapter gains a `flaky` mode
  (`AGENTFLOW_ECHO_FAIL_N` env → fail first N calls) or a module-level counter;
  assert: retries=2 + fail-1 → ok with a retry log; retries=0 + fail-1 → null;
  retries cap honored (fail-3 + retries=1 → null after 1 retry).
- Assert permissionDenied and timeout are NOT retried.

## Problem

`agentflow run` blocks until completion. Claude's Workflow runs detached with a
journal — the model continues other work and checks back. Our journal already
persists everything needed; the gap is the process lifecycle surface.

## Scope

- `--detach`: spawn `bin/agentflow run <script> <same flags> --run-id <id>` as a
  detached, unref'd child; parent prints `run <id>` + the status command and
  exits 0 immediately. Run-id is generated in the PARENT (so it's known before
  the child boots) and passed via a hidden `--run-id` flag that runScript
  accepts in place of generating one.
- Detached child's stderr/stdout append to `.agentflow/runs/<id>.log`
  (the JSONL journal stays the structured record; the .log keeps raw harness
  output for debugging).
- `agentflow status <run-id>`: reads `.agentflow/runs/<id>.jsonl`; prints
  run-start fields, per-phase progress (calls settled/labels), whether
  run-end exists (reason + code), and last N events. Exits 0 on terminal
  `ok`, 1 on terminal `error`, 2 while running.
- `agentflow tail <run-id>`: streams new journal lines until run-end (poll
  500ms; exits with status's code).
- `agentflow list` exists — extend it to show latest run + state if cheap,
  else leave as-is.

## Non-scope

- No IPC/RPC beyond files; no daemon; no cancellation channel yet
  (kill the child PID by hand; a `--stop` that signals the PID recorded in
  run-start is a reasonable later add — PID journaled in this unit).
- Detach + SIGINT semantics: the detached child still installs its own
  signal handlers; the parent's exit doesn't signal it (detached session).

## Implementation

- `src/cli.mjs`: `--detach` branch before `runScript`; `--run-id` passthrough;
  `status`/`tail` commands.
- `src/runtime.mjs`: accept `opts.runId` (use instead of `Journal.newRunId()`);
  journal `pid` in run-start.
- `src/journal.mjs`: `Journal.summary(path)` → `{runStart, events, runEnd}`-
  shape helper for status/tail reuse.
- `agentflow.example.json` + SKILL.md flags line.

## Tests

- `tests/runtime.test.mjs`: opts.runId honored; status summary shape.
- `tests/cli.test.mjs` (new): spawn `bin/agentflow run --detach` on an echo
  script in tmpdir; assert parent exits fast with run id; poll journal until
  run-end; `status` exits 0; `tail` output contains the phase line.
- Keep the suite's no-subprocess-for-unit-tests convention: the only new
  subprocess is the detached CLI itself (echo adapter — no model calls).

# M5 — deterministic test surface + CI

## Problem

The suite is already deterministic (echo adapter, env-injected failures, seeded
journals, zero model calls), but four gaps remain: `npm test` is broken on
Node ≥22 (`node --test tests/` treats the positional as a glob →
MODULE_NOT_FOUND), nothing runs the suite automatically (no `.github/`),
adapter `spawnAgent` glue is untested end-to-end — codex's `-o lastMsgFile`
capture has zero coverage, the exact seam the via-wrap-contract learning
flagged — the openrouter fetch/parse path can't run without network, and the
retries test burns ~4s of real wall-clock backoff (83% of suite time).

## Scope

### In scope

- Fix the `npm test` entry point for Node ≥20.
- Fake-binary e2e coverage for every subprocess adapter's `spawnAgent`
  (devin, claude, codex, opencode, ori), including via-ori wrap-through.
- Injectable-fetch seam on the openrouter adapter + response-parse tests.
- Injectable `opts.sleep` on `runScript` for retry backoff and grace polls.
- GitHub Actions workflow running the suite on push/PR.
- Housekeeping: close superseded PR #2 and delete remote `feat/v1-runner`.

### Out of scope

- `--strict` lint pattern expansion (`Date()`, `crypto.randomInt`,
  `performance.now`, env/fs reads) — a policy decision, tracked as deferred.
- Coverage instrumentation (c8), fuzz/property tests of the journal loader.
- Any live-model or network-dependent test — determinism is the point.

## Requirements

- **R1.** `npm test` exits 0 on the engines floor (Node 20) through current.
- **R2.** Every harness adapter's `spawnAgent` runs end-to-end deterministically
  in tests — argv → spawn → classify → parse — with no real binary required.
- **R3.** No unit test waits on real backoff; suite wall time ~1s class.
- **R4.** CI runs the full suite on push/PR across the supported Node range.
- **R5.** PR #2 and `feat/v1-runner` are retired (content landed via #1 squash).

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — bare `node --test` in `package.json`.** Auto-discovery covers
  `tests/*.test.mjs` on every Node ≥18.13; verified locally on Node 26.7.0
  (47 tests discovered). Fewer moving parts than a glob form.
- **KTD2 — fake binaries on PATH, not recorded transcripts.** Stub executables

  `docs/solutions/agent-orchestration/via-wrap-contract.md` proved argv-only
  tests can't see. Transcript replay would need a DI refactor for less signal.
- **KTD3 — injectable seams, not monkey-patching.** `opts.sleep` on `runScript`
  and a test-only fetch override on openrouter keep production code honest and
  tests hermetic. Mutating `process.env.PATH` inside the spawn call needs no
  runtime change (spawnProcess already defaults `env` to `process.env`).
- **KTD4 — matrix `[20, 22, 24, 26]` on `ubuntu-latest`.** Engines floor through
