# M6 — ops parity: `--stop`, scripted smoke runner, runner worktrees

## Problem

`--detach` + `status`/`tail` (#6) shipped the journal-based process surface,
but three deferrals remain: there is no cancellation channel (plan-003
explicitly deferred `--stop`), the v0.2-plan `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs`
was never written so the adapter matrix is manual and irreproducible, and
worktree isolation stayed backlog — parallel coding agents all share the
caller cwd, which collides the moment a workflow runs file-mutating stages.

## Scope

### In scope

- `agentflow stop <run-id>` — SIGTERM the journaled pid; runtime's existing
  drain/grace path journals `run-end: interrupted` itself.
- Orphan detection in `status`/`list`: pid dead + no `run-end` → `orphaned`,
  not `running`.
- `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs` — matrix-driven live smoke emitting markdown
  rows for `docs/smoke-matrix.md`.
- `worktree: 'auto'` on `agent()` — runner-provisioned git worktree per call,
  journaled; `agentflow clean` reclaims worktrees of ended runs.

### Out of scope

- RPC/daemon anything — file-and-signal only, same as detach.
- Merge-back/collection of worktree contents — the workflow script owns
  deciding what to do with each checkout (a later "collect" primitive).
- `agentflow clean` GC heuristics beyond "run ended" — no age/size policies.
- Provider-side cancellation of in-flight agent calls.

## Requirements

- **R1.** `agentflow stop <run-id>` reaches terminal state on a live run and
  exits 0; refuses to signal a pid whose start-time doesn't match the
  journal's `run-start.at` (pid-reuse guard).
- **R2.** `status`/`list` report `orphaned` when the journaled pid is dead and
  no `run-end` exists, pointing at `--resume`.
- **R3.** The smoke runner reproduces the adapter matrix on demand: per-adapter
  invocation, pass/fail, latency — cheap-first defaults, no premium models.
- **R4.** `agent(p, {worktree:'auto'})` runs the call with `cwd` set to a fresh
  `git worktree` of the containing repo, path journaled per call index.
- **R5.** `agentflow clean` removes journaled worktrees belonging to ended
  runs only — never a live run's checkout.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — signal the journaled pid; no pidfiles.** `run-start` already
  records `pid`. The reuse guard reads the process start-time
  (`/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux, `ps -o lstart=` fallback) and compares with
  `run-start.at` before SIGTERM — a mismatched pid is someone else's process.
- **KTD2 — worktrees persist past run-end; cleanup is explicit.** A worktree's
  value is the agent's work in it — auto-deleting at run-end could silently
  drop uncollected work. `agentflow clean` is the operator-visible reclaim.
- **KTD3 — `'auto'` is runner-owned; `true` stays adapter-native.** Codex's
  existing `--worktree` mapping is untouched. The runner consumes only the
  literal `'auto'` (converts to `spec.cwd` before the adapter sees it), so a
  codex call never gets both mechanisms.
- **KTD4 — smoke runner emits rows, not doc rewrites.** `smoke-matrix.md`
  stays human-curated; the script's job is reproducible invocation and
  measurement — re-run, paste rows. OR rows inherit `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
  from the caller env (workspace rule: eval spend routes via the orchestral
  key, never `openrouter/default`).

## Implementation Units

### U1. `agentflow stop` + orphan detection

**Goal:** live runs are stoppable; dead-pid journals read as orphaned.

**Requirements:** R1, R2

**Dependencies:** none

**Files:** `src/cli.mjs`, `tests/cli.test.mjs`, `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`

**Approach:** `stopCmd` loads the journal — ended → print end reason and exit
0 (already terminal); alive → read `runStart.pid`, liveness-check
(`process.kill(pid, 0)`), compare start-time vs `runStart.at` (refuse on
mismatch), `SIGTERM`, poll the journal until `run-end` or a grace+10s bound.
Exit 0 on reaching terminal, 1 on failure-to-stop, 2 on unknown run-id.
`statusCmd`/`list`: when no `run-end`, check pid liveness — dead →
`orphaned (pid N dead — resume: agentflow run <script> --resume <id>)`,
exit 2. SKILL.md gains stop/orphan/clean rows.

**Test scenarios:**

- Detached echo run (`AGENTFLOW_ECHO_SLOW` large) → `stop` → journal has
  `run-end: interrupted`, child pid gone; exit 0.
- `stop` on an ended run → prints reason, exit 0; unknown id → clean exit 2.
- Orphan: hand-write journal with a dead pid + no run-end → `status` prints
  `orphaned`; `stop` reports nothing-to-kill + `--resume` hint, no signal.
- Pid reuse: journal `runStart.pid` pointed at a live unrelated `sleep`
  process started after `run-start.at` → stop refuses, the process survives.

**Verification:** no zombie `--detach` runs; a crashed child can't be mistaken
for running.

### U2. `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs`

**Goal:** the live adapter matrix is one command away and reproducible.

**Requirements:** R3

**Dependencies:** none

**Files:** `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs` (new), `docs/smoke-matrix.md` (header
note), `README.md` (one line)

**Approach:** in-file row config `{name, harness, via?, model?, notes}` —
defaults mirror the v0.2 cheap-first matrix (devin `swe-2-medium`, ori +
openrouter + via-ori harnesses on `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash`, echo). Per row: probe
binary first (missing → `FAIL (not on PATH)` row, not a crash), spawn
`bin/agentflow run <script> --harness <h> [--via <v>] -- <model>` (default
script `examples/smoke.mjs`), 120s timeout, capture first-line text +
latency. Output: markdown table rows + `--json` for machine use; `--only
<csv>` filters rows. No secrets handled — env inherited.

**Test scenarios:**

- `--only echo` completes free and prints a PONG row.
- A row whose binary is absent → `FAIL (not on PATH)` row, script continues.
- Non-zero agentflow exit → row records fail + trimmed stderr line.
- `--json` emits a parseable array of `{name, harness, ok, latencyMs, text}`.

**Verification:** one invocation reproduces the 2026-10-09 matrix rows; rows
paste cleanly into `docs/smoke-matrix.md`.

### U3. `worktree: 'auto'` runner worktrees + `agentflow clean`

**Goal:** a call can demand its own checkout; reclaim is explicit.

**Requirements:** R4, R5

**Dependencies:** none

**Files:** `src/runtime.mjs`, `src/journal.mjs`, `src/cli.mjs`,
`tests/runtime.test.mjs`, `tests/cli.test.mjs`, `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`

**Approach:** inside the pool task (journal-before-slot-release invariant
holds), when `spec.worktree === 'auto'`: resolve repo root via `git -C <cwd>
rev-parse --show-toplevel` (failure → that call settles null with a

# M7 — distribution: visibility flip, verified installs, npm decision

## Problem

The README advertises `plugin marketplace add duketopceo/agentflow` for
claude/codex and `plugins install` for devin/opencode — all of which fail for
anyone without GitHub auth while the repo is `PRIVATE`. The v0.2 R9
visibility gate never got an answer, npm publish was deferred without a
decision, and `package.json` still says `"private": true`. Everything
agent-doable lands in this milestone; the two human gates are explicit stops,
not blockers.

## Scope

### In scope

- Publish-readiness prep: package manifest files/whitelist, name decision,
  README truth pass against actual visibility.
- GATE: repo visibility flip to public + workspace security standard applied
  (PR+1-review branch protection, fork-PR approval).
- Post-flip verification: each advertised install path run once from a
  scratch dir, manifests fixed until they work.
- GATE: npm publish — scoped name, or documented "not published" — decided
  and closed either way.

### Out of scope

- Third-party/official marketplace catalogs (Claude, Codex) — self-hosted
  manifests only.
- Release automation (release-please/changesets), docs site, installers.
- Any paid promotion, announcement, or growth work.

## Requirements

- **R1.** README install matrix is truthful about visibility at every step —
  no claim survives that a stranger can't execute.
- **R2.** The public flip is immediately followed by the workspace repo
  standard: default-branch protection (PR + 1 review, no force-push/delete)
  and `first_time_contributors` fork-PR approval — free GitHub tier cannot
  set API branch protection on private repos, so the flip is what unlocks
  the standard.
- **R3.** Each advertised install path is verified once from a clean scratch
  dir post-flip; failures fix the manifest, not the docs.
- **R4.** npm gets a definitive answer: published scoped name or an explicit
  "not published" note — never silently `"private": true` forever.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — gates are pauses, not blockers.** Prep and doc-truth work lands
  before either gate; an `lfg` run stops cleanly at the flip/publish actions
  with exact commands + rollback noted.
- **KTD2 — scoped name if published.** `agentflow` is likely squatted on npm;
  check `npm view agentflow` at implementation and default
  `@duketopceo/agentflow` with `publishConfig.access: public`. No-publish is
  a documented outcome, not a failure.
- **KTD3 — verify from a stranger's position.** Scratch tmp dir, no local
  clone assumptions — the exact resolution path a foreign harness runs.
- **KTD4 — flip unlocks protection, so they travel together.** Private free-
  tier repos can't receive API branch protection (noted in
  `docs/solutions/agent-orchestration/pooled-subprocess-agents-invariants.md`);
  the audit/fix step is part of the same unit as the flip, not a follow-up.

## Implementation Units

**Goal:** package manifest is publish-ready; docs never overclaim.

**Requirements:** R1, R4

**Dependencies:** none

**Requirements:** R2

**Dependencies:** U1

**Human action:** `gh repo edit duketopceo/agentflow --visibility public`,

# M8 — OpenRouter batch adapter: async jobs for latency-tolerant calls

## Problem

OpenRouter's Batch API is real and documented: `POST /api/v1/batches` accepts
`{endpoint, model, requests: [{custom_id, body}]}`, returns `202` +
`status: validating`; `GET /batches/{id}` polls
`validating|in_progress|finalizing|completed|failed|expired|cancelling|
cancelled`; terminal batches carry `results` keyed by `custom_id`. Pricing is
~40–60% off for ≤24h latency-tolerant work — the biggest untapped cost lever
in `docs/research/orchestration-economics.md`. Agentflow can't reach it: the
sync `spawnAgent` contract has no one-job-per-N-requests shape.

## Scope

### In scope

- `batch(specs)` script global on `--harness openrouter`: one submit → poll →
  array aligned to input (null per failed `custom_id`).
- Journal `batch` record `{batch_id, indices, hash}` — mid-poll interrupts
  resume by re-polling the existing id, never resubmitting.
- Abort-aware, bounded polling (defaults 15s interval, 2h overall — OR window
  is 24h; overridable per call + `agentflow.json`).
- `openrouter` adapter only; other harnesses fail fast with a clear error.
- Live verification run on a cheap `:batch` model (manual, non-CI).

### Out of scope

- Two-phase cross-run submit/collect — v1 batch() is a slower call, not a
  new lifecycle (deferred until real usage demands it).
- `provider.only` pinning, `allow_fallbacks` opts — submit uses OR's default
  cheapest-eligible routing.
- Non-`/v1/chat/completions` endpoints (`/responses`, `/messages`,
  `/embeddings`).
- Mixed-model fan-out — the API is one `model` per batch; v1 requires all
  items share one model.
- Batch `DELETE`/server-side cancel on `--stop`.

## Requirements

- **R1.** `batch(specs)` resolves to an array aligned to input order; failed
  or missing `custom_id`s settle `null`.
- **R2.** Each item consumes a normal call index — positional `--resume`
  accounting is unchanged.
- **R3.** Resume after mid-poll interrupt re-polls the journaled `batch_id`;
  a second `POST /batches` is never sent for the same index range + request
  content.
- **R4.** `batch()` on a non-batch adapter aborts the run before submitting,
  naming the constraint.
- **R5.** Poll loop honors `spec.signal` (SIGINT drain) and a deadline
  (`batchTimeoutMs`, default 2h; `batchPollMs`, default 15s — per-call opt +
  `agentflow.json`).
- **R6.** Terminal `failed`/`expired` → all items `null` with the batch
  error; per-request errors inside `completed` → those indices `null`.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — `batch(specs)` is its own global, not an `agent()` opt.** The API
  is one job per N requests; a `batch:true` opt would emit 1-request batches
  — no savings, wrong semantics. Array-in/array-out mirrors `parallel()`.
- **KTD2 — blocking-poll v1; two-phase deferred.** `batch()` as a slow call
  preserves call-order determinism and resume; the journal record covers the
  interrupt case. A detached collect-later API is backlog.
- **KTD3 — journal `batch` at submit, `agent` per item at collect — inside
  the pool task.** Same journal-before-slot-release invariant as sync calls
  (docs/solutions/agent-orchestration/pooled-subprocess-agents-invariants.md);
  per-item `agent` records keep positional replay identical.
- **KTD4 — schema stays prompt-level.** Batch request bodies reuse
  `buildBody` + `withSchemaPrompt`; native `response_format` is a later
  optimization.
- **KTD5 — same injectable-fetch seam as M5 U3.** Tests fake `/batches`
  responses without network; if this plan runs before M5, implement the
  minimal `fetchImpl` seam here (cross-plan dependency noted in U1).

## Implementation Units

### U1. openrouter batch client

**Goal:** adapter speaks `/batches` submit + poll + result mapping.

**Requirements:** R6 (partial), R4 prerequisite

**Dependencies:** M5 U3's `fetchImpl` seam, or implement it here if this plan
lands first

**Files:** `src/adapters/openrouter.mjs`, `tests/openrouter.test.mjs`

**Approach:** `supportsBatch: true` on the adapter; `submitBatch(model,
items)` → POST `{endpoint:'/v1/chat/completions', model, requests}` with
`custom_id: 'c<i>'` per item; `getBatch(id)` → GET. Uniform model enforced at
submit boundary: all items share one model or the caller errored earlier.
Same auth header + `fetchImpl` seam as the sync path.

**Test scenarios:**

- Submit body shape matches the API doc (endpoint, model, custom_id-keyed
  requests).
- `400` on a model with no `:batch` endpoint → error names the model.
- `401`/`403` → `permissionDenied:true`; `404` (`.only` mismatch class) →
  clear message, non-retryable.
- `getBatch` passes through status + `results`/`error` verbatim.

**Verification:** client functions are pure-ish and fully covered by faked
fetch; no network in tests.

### U2. `batch()` runtime global + journal resume

**Goal:** scripts get one new global with identical settle/resume semantics.

**Requirements:** R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6

**Dependencies:** U1

**Files:** `src/runtime.mjs`, `src/journal.mjs`, `tests/runtime.test.mjs`

**Approach:** `batch(specs)` — guarded by `adapter.supportsBatch` else throw
`batch() requires --harness openrouter` (run-end `error`, before submit).
Each item takes `i = callIndex++` (counts against `maxAgents`). Inside one
pool slot: uniform-model check → `submitBatch` → journal `{type:'batch',
batch_id, firstI, count, hash}` where `hash` canonicalizes the request array
→ poll `getBatch` on `batchPollMs` with `opts.sleep` until terminal or
`batchTimeoutMs`/abort → on `completed`, journal one `agent` record per item
(`ok`/error per `custom_id` result), resolve aligned array; on
`failed`/`expired`, journal per-item errors with the batch reason. Resume:
`Journal.load` exposes a pending batch record; when the replayed `batch()`
consumes the same `firstI..firstI+count` range and hashes equal → re-poll the
existing `batch_id` (zero resubmits); hash mismatch → warn + submit fresh.

**Test scenarios:**

- Fake fetch: POST once (`202 validating`) → GET `in_progress` → GET
  `completed` with results → array aligned, per-item `agent` records at the
  right indices; assert exactly one POST.
- `sleep` injected → poll loop instant in tests.
- Resume: seed journal `{type:'batch'}` pending + matching hash → second run
  polls existing id — still exactly one POST total; mismatched hash → new
  submit.
- Terminal `failed`/`expired` → all items `null`, error carries the reason.
- `completed` with per-request error on `c1` → index 1 `null`, others ok.
- Non-openrouter adapter → clean run error, zero fetch calls.
- Mixed per-item models → clear error before submit.
- Abort mid-poll → `run-end: interrupted`; batch record stays pending for
  resume.

**Verification:** positional resume semantics identical to sync calls;
interrupt can never double-spend a batch.

### U3. Docs + skill surface

**Goal:** `batch()` is discoverable and honestly scoped in the skill.

**Requirements:** R4 (documentation)

**Dependencies:** U2

**Files:** `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`, `README.md`,
`agentflow.example.json`

**Approach:** globals table gains `batch` with the uniform-model + openrouter-
only constraints; cost section notes ~40–60% off vs sync for
latency-tolerant stages, ≤24h window; `agentflow.example.json` shows
`batchPollMs`/`batchTimeoutMs` if the config keys land.

**Test expectation:** none — docs only; verified by U4's real run following
the documented invocation.

**Verification:** a fresh agent reading SKILL.md can produce a correct
`batch()` call without reading adapter source.

### U4. Live verification (manual, non-CI)

**Goal:** one real cheap batch proves the wire contract end-to-end.

**Requirements:** R1 (live)

**Dependencies:** U2

**Files:** `examples/batch-smoke.mjs` (new), `docs/smoke-matrix.md` (row)

**Approach:** `batch-smoke.mjs` submits 3 trivial prompts on
`z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` (its `:batch` variant), run manually with
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the orchestral eval key per workspace spend rules.
Record latency + cost as a smoke-matrix row; update the openrouter adapter
comment (`:batch` now supported via `batch()`).

**Test scenarios:**

- Run completes: 3/3 results aligned, journal shows one `batch` record +
  three `agent` records; cost row recorded.
- Interrupt mid-poll + `--resume` → completes without a second POST (checked
  against OR request logs or timing).

**Verification:** smoke-matrix has a verified batch row with date + model +
spend.

## Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- Two-phase cross-run collect (`batchSubmit`/`batchCollect` script
  primitives); detached batch polling.
- `provider.only`/`allow_fallbacks` opts; mixed-model auto-grouping into N
  batches; non-chat-completions endpoints.
- `DELETE /batches/{id}` on `agentflow stop`/SIGINT for spend hygiene.
- Batch support on non-openrouter providers if demand appears.

# Program roadmap

## Problem frame

agentflow runs one workflow script across `devin`, `claude`, `codex`,
`opencode`, `ori` and a direct `openrouter` adapter. v0.2 on `main` has the
runner, journal, `--resume`, `--cache`, `--via ori`, `--detach`, retries and a
live smoke matrix. Two PRs are in flight (M5 tests + CI, M6 ops parity). The
landscape research shows three gaps against what users of Claude's native
workflows, Temporal and LangGraph expect: resume that checks what it replays,
enforced determinism, and scripts that are genuinely portable to and from
Claude's runtime. This plan orders the remaining work and says where to build
less.

Scope: a program-level roadmap. Individual units become their own plans when
picked up. Application code is out of scope for this PR.

## Status key

`done` merged on `main` · `in-review` open PR · `planned` not started ·
`candidate` worth doing only if the stated trigger is met.

## Now

### U1. Land M5: deterministic suite and CI (PR #7)
- **Status:** in-review. Evidence: PR #7 body reports 65 tests, fakebin e2e
  stubs for all five CLIs, `spec.fetchImpl` seam, CI on Node 20/22/24/26.
  On `main` today `npm test` exits 1 under Node 26.7 because `node --test tests/`
  is treated as a path (verified in this pass: `npm test` exit 1, bare
  `node --test` exit 0, 47/47 pass).
- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Verification:** CI green on the four Node versions; `npm test` exit 0 locally.
- **Difficulty:** easy. It is reviewed and review fixes are applied.
- **Feasibility:** blockers are review latency and the unchecked "CI green" box.
  `engines` bump to `>=20.3` is a (small) breaking change for Node 20.0-20.2.
- **Simpler alternative:** if fakebin stubs are judged too heavy, keep only the
  `package.json` fix (`node --test`) and the CI file, which is most of the value.
  Candidate to delete: nothing on `main`; the stubs in `tests/fakebin/` are the
  new surface.

### U2. Land M6: ops parity (PR #8)
- **Status:** in-review. Evidence: PR #8 body (stop, clean, orphan detection,
  `worktree: 'auto'`, `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs`, 73 tests).
- **Dependencies:** U1 (both edit `.github/workflows/test.yml` and
  `package.json`). Per the stacked-PR rule, retarget to `main` and rebase; do not stack.
- **Verification:** `node --test` green; run `node scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs --only echo`.
- **Difficulty:** medium. Large diff touching `cli.mjs`, `journal.mjs`, `runtime.mjs`;
  already 11-persona reviewed.
- **Feasibility:** `rm -rf`-class code (`clean`) and pid signalling need the
  containment checks the PR claims; live smoke rows need credentials and spend.
- **Simpler alternative:** `agentflow clean` could be `git worktree prune` plus a
  documented `rm -r .agentflow/worktrees`; the pid-identity check in `stop` is the
  part worth keeping. `scripts/smoke-harnesses.mjs` duplicates the hand-run table in
  `docs/smoke-matrix.md`; keep the script, generate the table from it, delete the prose.

### U3. Replay guard: refuse stale results on `--resume`
- **Status:** done. Evidence: `src/runtime.mjs` replays `prior.settled.get(i)` by
  call index with no check that the prompt matches; Claude's runtime reruns from the
  first differing prompt (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows#resume-after-a-pause).
- **Dependencies:** U2 (journal epochs live there).
- **Verification:** new runtime test: edit a prompt between runs and assert the
  changed call and everything after it re-executes; journal records a prompt hash.
- **Difficulty:** medium. Small code change, but it changes journal format and needs
  a compatibility path for existing journals.
- **Feasibility:** none external. Decision needed: rerun everything after the first
  mismatch (Claude's rule, wasteful) or only mismatched calls (cheaper, but order
  assumptions break). Start with Claude's rule for parity.
- **Simpler alternative:** make `--cache` (content-keyed, already built) the default
  resume mechanism and drop positional replay entirely. That deletes
  the index-matching path in `runtime.mjs` and removes a whole class of stale-replay bugs, at
  the cost of cache files holding results between runs.

### U4. Script contract parity with Claude's native workflows
- **Status:** done. Evidence: Claude scripts end with `return <value>` and read
  `args` as structured data; agentflow's `fn(...)` result is discarded in `runScript`
  and `args` is always a string array. Claude also supports per-agent `stallMs`.
  `workflows/deep-research.mjs` calls `process.exit(2)` on bad input, which Claude's
  sandbox would not allow.
- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Verification:** a Claude-style script (copied from the docs example) runs
  unchanged under `--harness echo`; its `return` value is printed and journaled;
  `--args-json` yields structured `args`.
- **Difficulty:** medium. Changes touch `runtime.mjs` and `cli.mjs`; the risky
  part is deciding the output surface for the return value.
- **Feasibility:** Claude's contract is documented but not versioned; it may move
  (it changed between 2026-10-08 and today: `/workflow-authoring`, `stallMs`).
  Pin to a documented subset rather than chase it.
- **Simpler alternative:** document the three gaps in SKILL.md and ship one
  conformance script instead of changing the runtime. Cheaper, but the main
  differentiator (portability) stays aspirational.

### U5. Close distribution: npm decision and truthful install docs
- **Status:** planned (M7 plan 003). Evidence: the repo is already public
  (`gh api`: `visibility: public`), so the visibility gate in plan 003 is stale;
  `package.json` still has `"private": true`. README install matrix was not
  verified from a clean directory in this pass.
- **Dependencies:** U1.
- **Verification:** each install row in README run once from a scratch dir; `npm pack --dry-run`
  file list reviewed.
- **Difficulty:** easy for docs, medium if publishing (human gate).
- **Feasibility:** npm name `agentflow` may be squatted; scoped name needs an org;
  the Claude and Codex marketplace schemas are unverified against real installs.
- **Simpler alternative:** do not publish to npm. Keep `git clone` + `bin/agentflow`
  and the plugin manifests, and record "not published" explicitly (plan 003's KTD4
  allows this). Delete `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` if the Codex install path
  cannot be verified.

## Next

### U6. Determinism enforced at runtime, not by regex
- **Status:** done. Evidence: `lintDeterminism` in `runtime.mjs` is a regex over
  source text and only runs with `--strict`; Claude and Temporal enforce at runtime.
- **Dependencies:** U4 (shares the script sandbox).
- **Verification:** a script calling `Date.now()` fails with a clear error under
  default settings; `--allow-nondeterminism` opts out.
- **Difficulty:** easy. Shadow `Date`, `Math` and `crypto` as `AsyncFunction` parameters.
- **Feasibility:** the script runs in the host process via `AsyncFunction` (no real sandbox);
  shadowing is advisory, not a security boundary. State that plainly.
- **Simpler alternative:** delete `lintDeterminism` and the `--strict` flag once
  runtime enforcement ships (about 15 lines in `src/runtime.mjs`, plus its tests
  and the `strict` key in `agentflow.example.json`).

### U7. Validated structured output
- **Status:** planned. Evidence: only codex uses a native schema; every other adapter
  does `withSchemaPrompt` + `extractJson`, and a parse miss becomes `null`
  (`base.mjs`). Claude validates and retries up to five times.
- **Dependencies:** U1 (needs fakebin tests).
- **Verification:** fakebin stub returns invalid JSON once then valid; call resolves
  with the valid result; a permanently invalid reply yields `null` with an error naming the schema failure.
- **Difficulty:** medium.
- **Feasibility:** a JSON-Schema validator is a new dependency (the repo has one
  runtime dep today); a 60-line subset validator avoids it but is a maintenance
  liability.
- **Simpler alternative:** one repair retry that re-prompts with the parse error,

# agentflow watch — live animated run view

## Problem

`agentflow tail <run-id>` streams journal events as text lines — a log, not a
view. There is no way to see a run's *shape* while it moves: which calls are
queued, which are in-flight, how far a batch has gotten. Two gaps block it:

1. **No progress signal.** The journal only records *settled* calls
   (`agent` records are appended on completion) plus `batch`/`run-start`/
   `run-end`. An in-flight call emits nothing — a renderer reading today's
   journal can show "settled 4/11" but never "index 5 has been running 40s".
2. **No renderer.** `tail` prints one line per settled event; nothing keeps
   a spatial layout (per-index lanes, batch progress, elapsed clock) alive
   on screen.

## Scope

### In scope

- Journal progress records: `in-flight` on call start (per index; batch
  marks all its item indices), `batch-poll` per getBatch cycle
  (`{batch_id, status, pending, settled, total, at}`).
- `agentflow watch [run-id]` — zero-dep ANSI TUI that folds the journal
  event stream into a live per-index state view. No arg → newest journal in
  cwd's `.agentflow/runs/`.
- Non-TTY fallback: when stdout isn't a TTY, emit the same event stream
  `tail` does (watch IS tail with a renderer on top).
- Exit on `run-end` showing the final frame; return `endCode(ended)`.

### Out of scope

- Interactive input (pause/reorder/kill from inside the view) — `stop`
  already owns run control.
- Multi-run or historical browse view.
- Web/GUI dashboard — the journal is the data source; a web view is a later
  consumer of the same records.
- Rendering partial stdout/stderr content of in-flight calls — the journal
  doesn't carry streaming output and won't start.
- Editing the run — watch is strictly read-only.

## Requirements

- **R1.** Every call emits `{type:'in-flight', i, label, model, at}` before
  spawn; every `batch()` item index emits one at submit time. `batch-poll`
  records carry status + counts on each poll.
- **R2.** New record types never affect resume: `Journal.load` keeps
  `settled`/`batches`/`ended` semantics identical (in-flight is not `agent`;
  verified — `load` ignores unknown types).
- **R3.** `watch` derives per-index latest state by folding the event
  stream: `in-flight` → `agent` (settled) or dead-at-`run-end`; batch items
  show poll status until their own `agent` record lands.
- **R4.** TTY: alternate-screen ANSI view, ~4fps, redraws on journal change;
  per-index lane, batch lane with poll progress, elapsed clock, settle
  meter. Small terminals truncate gracefully.
- **R5.** Non-TTY output is byte-for-byte the `tail` event stream (drop-in
  for scripts/pipes).
- **R6.** `watch` exits on `run-end` with the run's end code; missing
  run-id/journal exits 2 with a clear message; orphaned pid (dead run, no
  `run-end`) is surfaced in the header, not hung on forever — same check as
  `tail`/`stop` already do.

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — progress lives in the journal, not a sidecar file.** The journal
  is already the append-only event log every consumer reads; `in-flight`/
  `batch-poll` are just two more record types. Backward-compatible by
  construction (`load` skips unknown types), and `--resume` on an older
  journal simply has no progress records to show.
- **KTD2 — watch is a separate command, not a `run` flag.** Runs can be
  `--detach`ed, resumed, or watched from a second terminal; a renderer
  bound to the run process could do none of that. `--detach`'s hint line
  updates to suggest `watch`.
- **KTD3 — zero-dep ANSI, same re-read loop as `tail`.** No blessed/ink
  dep: cursor-home + clear-line redraw at ~250ms (or on `fs.watch` of the
  journal), reading the whole file each tick like `statusCmd` does —
  journals are small and append-only.
- **KTD4 — state is derived, never stored.** Watch recomputes the per-index
  state table from the event stream each frame; no mutable view model to
  drift out of sync with the journal.

## Implementation Units

### U1. Journal progress records

**Goal:** in-flight work and batch polls are visible to journal readers.

**Requirements:** R1, R2

**Files:** `src/runtime.mjs`, `src/journal.mjs`, `tests/journal.test.mjs` (or
batch/runtime tests)

**Approach:** append `{type:'in-flight', i, label, model, at}` at pool-task
start (before spawn); for `batch()`, emit one per item index at submit and
`{type:'batch-poll', batch_id, status, pending, settled, total, at}` on each
`getBatch` cycle (cheap lines — polls are ≥1s apart). `Journal.load` gains
`inFlight: Map` + `lastBatchPoll` in its meta for `status`/`watch` consumers
(existing `settled`/`batches`/`ended` unchanged). Resume: records from a
prior epoch are stale context only — replay semantics read `agent` records
exactly as today.

**Test scenarios:**

- Run a script: journal contains `in-flight` records preceding each `agent`
  record for the same index; batch items all emit `in-flight` at submit.
- `Journal.load` on a journal containing the new types: `settled` map
  identical to before, `batches` unaffected, `inFlight` exposes open items.
- Resume on a journal with stale `in-flight` + `batch-poll` records: replay
  is unchanged (settled replayed, unsettled re-run).
- `batch-poll` reflects getBatch statuses in order.

**Verification:** resume/replay tests green; load meta shape additive only.

### U2. `agentflow watch` renderer

**Goal:** a live animated view of any run from its journal.

**Requirements:** R3, R4, R5, R6

**Dependencies:** U1 (progress records) — view still works without them, just
never shows in-flight lanes

**Files:** `src/cli.mjs` (watchCmd), `src/watch.mjs` (new — pure fold +
render), `tests/watch.test.mjs`

**Approach:** `watch.mjs` exports two pure functions: `foldState(records)`
→ `{meta, lanes: [{i, label, state, secs}], batch: {…}, done}` and
`renderFrame(state, {now, width, spinner})` → string. cli.mjs adds
`agentflow watch [run-id]`: resolve newest journal when no arg; TTY →
alt-screen + `hideCursor`, tick ~250ms reloading journal, `renderFrame`
each tick, on `run-end` show final frame then restore screen and return
`endCode`; non-TTY → the `tail` event stream verbatim. Spinner frames +
elapsed use an injectable `now`/`tick` for tests. Header shows run-id,
script, harness, elapsed, pid-liveness (same `pidState` check `stop` uses).
Lanes: `◌ queued → ◐ in-flight (age) → ● ok / ○ null`; batch lane shows
`status`, `pending`/`settled` counts from the latest `batch-poll`, and the
claim-ticket `batch_id` (truncated).

**Test scenarios:**

- `foldState` on a recorded sequence: queued→in-flight→ok transitions per
  index; batch in-flight → per-item settle; `run-end` marks done; stale
  in-flight with `run-end:interrupted` shows abandoned.
- `renderFrame` deterministic output for a fixed state + `now` + tick —
  snapshot-assert the frame (labels, lane states, batch progress, elapsed).
- Non-TTY mode prints exactly the `tail` event lines for the same journal.
- `watch` on a missing run-id → exit 2, clear message.
- Child-process e2e: run script + `watch` concurrently → run completes,
  watch exits 0, captured frames show at least one `in-flight` lane then
  final `● ok` lanes.
- Small width → no crash, lanes truncated not wrapped.

**Verification:** every render is pure; the only I/O is journal read +
stdout write.

### U3. Docs + ops surface

**Goal:** discoverable in the places agents/users look.

**Requirements:** R4 (documentation)

**Dependencies:** U2

**Files:** `README.md`, `skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`, `src/cli.mjs` USAGE +
`--detach` hint

**Approach:** ops table gains `watch`; `--detach` prints `watch:` hint
(alongside existing `tail`/`status` lines); SKILL.md notes in-flight/
batch-poll records exist in journals for consumers.

**Verification:** `agentflow` USAGE text + SKILL.md commands table agree
with the built flags (covered by existing cli help test if present).

## Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- Watch inside `run` (`--watch` flag spawning the view on the same run).
- Multi-run overview; finished-run playback mode (`--speed` replay).
- Web dashboard consuming the same journal records.
- Per-call live output streaming (requires journals to carry output chunks —
  a separate decision).

# openai + anthropic direct adapters — first-party batch APIs

## Problem

`batch()` has three working backends (openrouter `/batches`, devin `/v3`
sessions, perplexity `/v1/async/sonar`). OpenAI and Anthropic both run
first-party batch APIs at ~50% off — the same discount class as OR — but
the `claude`/`codex` adapters can't reach them: those adapters wrap CLIs,
and a subprocess is synchronous by nature. The fix is two direct-API
adapters implementing the established batch contract — verified entirely
without live calls per the no-spend constraint.

## Scope

### In scope

- `openai` adapter: sync `agent()` on `POST /v1/chat/completions` +
  `supportsBatch` on the Batches API.
- `anthropic` adapter: sync `agent()` on `POST /v1/messages` +
  `supportsBatch` on Message Batches.
- Same adapter contract as openrouter/devin/perplexity: `buildBody`,
  `batchBody`, `submitBatch`, `getBatch`, `batchResultMap` (shared from
  `base.mjs`), `batchItemResult`, `probe`, `supportsBatch`.
- Env seams: `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`;
  `AGENTFLOW_OPENAI_BASE`/`AGENTFLOW_ANTHROPIC_BASE` base overrides;
  `fetchImpl` throughout.
- Deterministic tests only — zero live calls, zero spend.

### Out of scope

- **Live verification — deferred behind a human gate** (explicit user
  constraint: don't use these providers). smoke-matrix rows are recorded as
  deterministic-only; a live run happens only if the user opts in later.
- `codex`/`claude` CLI adapters gaining batch — impossible by construction
  (no async surface); these API adapters are the answer, not CLI flags.
- File/embedding/fine-tune endpoints; tool-use parameters; vision payloads.
- Batch cancel/delete on `agentflow stop` (already deferred for OR/devin).
- OpenAI `output_file_id` streaming partial results mid-run.

## Requirements

- **R1.** Both adapters implement the full batch contract; `batch()` on
  `--harness openai`/`--harness anthropic` produces index-aligned arrays
  through the unchanged runtime path.
- **R2.** `agent()` sync calls work on both adapters with the standard
  `{text, json}` result; `schema:` stays prompt-level via `withSchemaPrompt`.
- **R3.** Auth is env-only (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); missing
  key fails cleanly on every entrypoint; 401/403 → `permissionDenied`.
- **R4.** Resume semantics preserved: journaled `batch_id` re-polls without
  resubmitting — identical to the other backends (composite id or single id
  as each API dictates).
- **R5.** All wire interactions injectable via `fetchImpl`; every test is
  network-free.
- **R6.** Per-item failures settle `null` only for that index (per-request
  error entries inside completed results; terminal-without-result items).

## Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — openai submit is two calls inside `submitBatch`.** OpenAI Batches
  require a JSONL upload first: `POST /v1/files` (multipart, `purpose:
  'batch'`, lines `{custom_id, method:'POST', url:'/v1/chat/completions',
  body}`) → `POST /v1/batches {input_file_id, endpoint, completion_window:
  '24h'}`. `submitBatch` does both and returns only the batch id — the file
  id is transient (a failed second call orphans a harmless upload). The
  journaled `batch_id` is just the batch id — resume re-polls it directly.
- **KTD2 — result collection happens inside `getBatch`.** OpenAI terminal
  `completed` batches expose `output_file_id` — `getBatch` fetches
  `GET /v1/files/{id}/content` (JSONL `{custom_id, response:{status_code,
  body}, error}`) and returns the normalized results array in one
  `{status:'completed', results}` response. Anthropic `ended` batches expose
  `results_url` — same inside-getBatch fetch+parse pattern. The runtime
  sees one uniform terminal shape.
- **KTD3 — anthropic quirks live in `buildBody`/`batchItemResult`.**
  `max_tokens` is required (default 8192, overridable per item); `system`
  stays out (schema instruction stays in the user message, consistent with
  the other adapters); response content blocks `[{type:'text',text}]` →
  `text`; per-item result `type` maps: `succeeded` → `message`, `errored`/
  `expired`/`canceled` → per-item error. Auth header is `x-api-key` +
  `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` (and `anthropic-beta:
  message-batches-2024-09-24` on the batches endpoints — include
  unconditionally; harmless if GA'd).
- **KTD4 — verify-at-implement-time list, not assumptions.** Unverified
  details are marked here and pinned by tests where possible; where the
  wire can't be checked without spend, the adapter comment + smoke-matrix
  row say so honestly: exact model slugs (defaults below), whether Message
  Batches still needs the beta header, OpenAI `output_file_id` presence on
  `expired` batches (partial results — v1 ignores them), and multipart
  upload field names (`purpose`, `file`).
- **KTD5 — defaults.** openai model default `gpt-4.1-mini`; anthropic model
  default `claude-haiku-4-5` — both cheap-tier placeholders to be confirmed
  at implement/live time, documented in the adapter comment like the others.

## Implementation Units

### U1. `anthropic` adapter

**Goal:** sync + batch contract on `api.anthropic.com`.

**Requirements:** R1–R6

**Files:** `src/adapters/anthropic.mjs`, `src/adapters/index.mjs`,
`tests/anthropic.test.mjs`

**Approach:** `spawnAgent` → `POST /v1/messages` `{model, max_tokens,
messages:[{role:'user',content}]}` → `{content:[{type:'text',text}]}`;
`batchBody` → `{custom_id, params:{model,max_tokens,messages}}` minus
custom_id (hash material = params); `submitBatch` → `POST
/v1/messages/batches {requests}` → `{id, processing_status}`; `getBatch` →
`GET /v1/messages/batches/{id}`: `in_progress`/`canceling` → keep polling;
`ended` → fetch `results_url`, parse JSONL → `results` array; per-item
`result.type` → `succeeded` → message body, others → `{error}`. Status
mapping to runtime: only `completed` triggers collect; expose `ended` as
`completed` in the getBatch return (`b.status` checked verbatim — map
`ended` → `'completed'` at the adapter boundary).

**Test scenarios:**

- Submit body: `requests` array with `custom_id` `c0..cN`, `params`
  carrying model/max_tokens/messages; `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`
  headers present.
- `getBatch`: `in_progress` → keep; `ended` + results_url → fetches JSONL,
  maps `succeeded`/`errored`/`expired` per `custom_id`.
- `spawnAgent`: text extraction, `max_tokens` default + override, schema
  prompt expansion, empty content → clean error, 401 → permissionDenied.
- Missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → clean error on all entrypoints.
- `batchItemResult`: message → `{text,json}`, error entry → errResult.

### U2. `openai` adapter

**Goal:** sync + batch contract on `api.openai.com`.

**Requirements:** R1–R6

**Files:** `src/adapters/openai.mjs`, `src/adapters/index.mjs`,
`tests/openai.test.mjs`

**Approach:** `spawnAgent` → `POST /v1/chat/completions` (same shape as
openrouter minus routing opts); `batchBody` → chat-completions body;
`submitBatch` → upload JSONL (`{custom_id, method, url, body}` lines) via
`POST /v1/files` → `POST /v1/batches` → `{id,status}`; `getBatch` →
`GET /v1/batches/{id}`: non-terminal → status passthrough; `completed` →
fetch `output_file_id` content, parse JSONL `{custom_id, response:
{status_code, body}, error}` → results; `failed|expired|cancelled` → batch
error to runtime. Multipart upload via `FormData`/`Blob` (Node 20 native).

**Test scenarios:**

- Submit performs exactly two calls: file upload (JSONL parses, custom_ids
  aligned, url `/v1/chat/completions`) then batch create (`input_file_id`,
  `completion_window: '24h'`); returns the batch id.
- `getBatch` on `completed` fetches output file once, maps per-custom_id
  `response.body`/`error` entries.
- Terminal `failed|expired` → batch-level error passthrough to runtime.
- `spawnAgent`/`batchItemResult`/missing-key/permissionDenied — same
  coverage as anthropic U1.

### U3. Runtime e2e + registry + docs

**Goal:** both adapters run through the real `batch()` path and are
discoverable.

**Requirements:** R1, R4

**Dependencies:** U1, U2

**Files:** `tests/batch.test.mjs` (two blocks), `README.md`,
`skills/agentflow/SKILL.md`, `docs/smoke-matrix.md`, `package.json`
(files whitelist check)

**Approach:** append `openai batch:` and `anthropic batch:` blocks mirroring
the perplexity block — e2e aligned results + journal records, resume
re-polls journaled id (zero new submits), per-item failure settles only
that index. SKILL.md adapter table + `batch` global row gain both rows with
the env keys; smoke-matrix gains **deterministic-only** rows explicitly
marked "live deferred — no-spend gate"; adapter comments carry the
verify-at-implement-time list from KTD4.

**Test scenarios:**

- Per adapter, the 3 e2e scenarios via `runScript` + `stubFetch`.
- `Object.keys(adapters)` test updated for +2 adapters.
- Docs: a fresh agent reading SKILL.md writes a correct `batch()` call on
  either new harness.

**Verification:** suite green; zero network assertions hold (no test makes
a real request — stubFetch throws on unstubbed calls).

## Deferred to Follow-Up Work

- **Live verification of both adapters** — human gate; smoke-matrix rows
  flip from "deterministic-only" to verified when opted in.
- Anthropic beta-header removal if GA; `system` param support; tool-use
  params; OpenAI partial results on `expired`.
- Batch cancel/delete on `stop` (cross-adapter, already deferred).
- A generic "provider list/reconcile" surface (OpenAI `GET /batches` list
  exists — same future `agentflow reconcile` idea as perplexity/devin).

## Risks

- **Wire-shape drift unverified live.** Mitigation: contract is identical
  to three working adapters; every field is unit-tested against the
  documented shape; honest "unverified live" marking in docs/comments; the
  live gate flips cheap (one env key + one run).
- **Model slug guesses.** Defaults are placeholders documented as such;
  wrong-slug errors surface cleanly through the existing error path.
- **Anthropic API surface details (beta header, results_url auth).** Tests
  pin the documented shape; if the live gate later shows drift, the fix is
  isolated to one adapter file.

# feat: OpenCode plugin for v1 and v2 from one package

## Product Contract

### Summary

Restore a working v1 tool surface alongside the v2 port, so one package serves every OpenCode user that can actually install a CLI — and so the install docs stop claiming a plugin exists only for a version nobody can run.

### Problem Frame

agentflow has shipped an OpenCode plugin that no user has successfully run.

The v1 plugin at `.opencode/plugins/agentflow.ts` read the child process through Bun's `` $`agentflow ${args}` `` helper and returned `.text()`. That captures **stdout only**. The runner writes every operator-relevant line to **stderr** — the phase markers, the per-lane `ok`/`fail` lines, the `[agentflow] run <run-id>` line, and the script's own `log()` output, which is how `workflows/deep-research.mjs` surfaces its synthesis. Verified directly against the current `main`:

```
=== STDOUT ONLY ===        (empty)
=== STDERR ONLY ===
[0.0s] [a] p -> ok (0.0s)
[0.0s] [a] SYNTHESIS_ON_LOG: echo[p]: say PONG
[agentflow] run 2026-10-11T08-48-18-e3406f18
```

So `agentflow_run` returned `""` on every successful run. A calling agent received no run-id, could not resume or stop the run, and on failure received only `ShellError: Failed with exit code 1` with the real reason discarded in stderr. No test covered the file: it is the only TypeScript file in a repo whose runtime is otherwise plain `.mjs`, and `grep -rl plugin tests/` returns nothing.

PR #19 (`feat/opencode-v2`, commit `73302f0`) ported the plugin to the OpenCode v2 contract and fixed the capture defect by moving to `execFile` and concatenating both streams. It also **deleted the v1 path outright**. That trade is correct on its own terms — v1 code does not run under v2 — but it leaves every currently-installable OpenCode with nothing, because v2 does not exist as a shipped CLI: `opencode-ai` tops out at `1.19.0`, and the installed binary is `1.18.33`.

The result is a branch whose CI is green without ever exercising the plugin, an install matrix that tells users to run a command that cannot succeed, and an untested v2 arm presented as working.

This plan keeps Devin's v2 arm and restores a v1 arm that captures stderr correctly, packaged so one install serves both.

### Requirements

- **R1.** One package exposes both implementations from a single default export — the dual-support shape the official v2 migration guide documents — so a single install serves v1 and v2 consumers.
- **R2.** The v1 arm registers `agentflow_run` and `agentflow_doctor`, returning non-empty text on success that contains the run-id and the script's own output.
- **R3.** Neither arm's success path can return an empty string, and neither may discard the failure reason when a run exits nonzero.
- **R4.** The v1 arm is exercisable on OpenCode `1.18.29+`; the v2 arm is preserved as Devin wrote it.
- **R5.** Install documentation is true for both versions, and states plainly that the v2 arm cannot be exercised until a v2 CLI ships.
- **R6.** The plugin's own contract is covered by tests that run in CI, so a future refactor cannot silently reintroduce an empty return.
- **R7.** `agentflow` remains on `PATH` as the only runtime requirement; the plugin adds no new install prerequisites.

### Success Criteria

- A v1 run through `agentflow_run` returns text containing the run-id; the same holds for the failure path, which returns the reason rather than a generic exit code.
- A test asserts a stub writing only to stderr still produces non-empty tool output — the specific regression that shipped.
- Neither install doc contains a command that cannot succeed on any released OpenCode.
- The v2 arm's unexercised status appears in the install notes, not only in a commit message.

### Scope Boundaries

**In scope:** the dual package shape, the v1 arm's tool registration and stream capture, dependency placement, tests for the plugin contract, and truthful install docs for both versions.

**Out of scope — non-goals for this plan:**

- Covering more of the CLI in the tool surface. `agentflow_run` and `agentflow_doctor` stay the only two tools; no detached-run lifecycle, no `start`/`status`/`stop` split, no result-retrieval verb. That is a separate design question with a separate answer.
- CI or lint work beyond what the new tests require.
- The OpenRouter usage/cost gap. Separately verified and separately real: the OpenRouter response carries `usage.cost` (USD) and `cost_details`, and `src/adapters/openrouter.mjs` discards them; `src/watch.mjs` reads `costUsd`, which no adapter sets. Unrelated to the plugin.
- Any change to the agentflow CLI's own output streams. The plugin must adapt to stderr, not the reverse.

**Deferred to follow-up work:**

- Deciding whether a result-retrieval verb should exist at all, given no CLI verb currently prints result text and the synthesis lives only in the JSONL journal.
- Replacing the exact dependency pin with a tested range across the whole manifest, once a live v2 install exists to test against.

### Key Decisions

- **Session-settled: cover both surfaces in one plan**, rather than picking v1 or v2. Chosen over a v2-only package, which would serve nobody installable today.
- **Session-settled: ship the plugin rather than skill-only.** The skill is the stronger surface and remains the primary one; this plan does not reopen that trade, and does not reduce skill coverage.
- **Session-settled: install fix and surface contract only.** Deliberately not a hardening pass.

## Planning Contract

### Key Technical Decisions

- **KTD1 — Dual export, not two packages.** Follow the migration guide's documented shape: one default export spreading `Plugin.define({id, setup})` for v2 alongside a v1 plugin function. Two packages would double the release surface and the manifests for no benefit; the guide states the APIs "remain separate" and that the shape does not translate hooks automatically, which is exactly the boundary wanted here — each arm keeps its native idiom and neither emulates the other.

- **KTD2 — The v1 arm captures stderr by construction, not by patch.** The defect was reading the wrong stream. Rather than append a stderr handler after the fact, the v1 arm uses the shell helper's combined-output path so no future edit can reintroduce a stdout-only read. The v2 arm's `execFile` + `${stdout}${stderr}` concatenation stays as Devin wrote it — it is already correct and matches the documented pattern.

- **KTD3 — Tool arguments are assembled by a shared pure function.** Both arms build argv identically today; duplicated assembly is how the two surfaces drifted in the first place. One exported helper produces the argv array from a spec object, so the two arms differ only in how they invoke it. This is what makes the shared contract testable without a live OpenCode.

- **KTD4 — Dependencies are scoped to where they are used.** The v1 arm needs `@opencode-ai/plugin`; the v2 arm needs `@opencode/plugin`. The v1 dependency goes back into the root manifest (the plugin is packaged from the repo root and `exports["./server"]` resolves there); the v2 SDK stays a peer dependency of the plugin subpackage rather than a root runtime dependency, so an installer who only needs the v2 path does not pull the v1 SDK. - **KTD5 — Tests target the contract, not the harness.** A stub binary writing only to stderr is the highest-value test here: it reproduces the shipped defect exactly without a live OpenCode, an API key, or a real run. Tool-registration shape is asserted by importing the plugin module and inspecting what it registers. This follows the existing `tests/fakebin/` pattern rather than inventing a second one.

- **KTD6 — Docs state the v2 arm's real status.** The install notes keep Devin's honest note that the v2 arm is written against the docs but not yet exercised, and add the v1 install path beside it. The README row stops advertising a single v2-only command.

- The dual-export shape documented in the v2 migration guide is the intended and supported mechanism, and "V1 object entrypoints are supported in OpenCode 1.18.29 and newer" applies to a TypeScript default export reached through the existing `exports["./server"]` entry.
- `exports["./server"]` remains the correct entry key for v1 resolution, and `plugins/agentflow/` remains the correct `::path:` target for v2 installs.
- The v2 tool-registration shape in `plugins/agentflow/index.ts` is correct as written. ### High-Level Technical Design

Two arms, one entry, one shared argument builder. Drawn from the current branch (`feat/opencode-v2`, `73302f0`) and the v1 plugin that commit deleted.

```
                    package default export
                            |
        +-------------------+-------------------+
        |                                       |
   v1 arm (runs on 1.18.29+)            v2 arm (runs on 2.x)
   @opencode-ai/plugin                  @opencode/plugin
   Plugin.define(...).spread            Plugin.define({id, setup})
   + server()                           |
        |                                       |
        |        +------------------------+     |
        +------->| shared argv builder    |<----+
                 | (pure, exported)       |
                 +------------------------+
                           |
                  argv: string[]
                           |
              +------------+-------------+
              |                          |
       v1: $ shell helper        v2: execFile
       combined output           stdout + stderr
              |                          |
              +------------+-------------+
                           |
                  non-empty text out
                  (run-id + script log)
```

The stderr contract is the load-bearing part, and it is asymmetric between the runner and every consumer of it:

```
  agentflow runner                 plugin consumer
  -----------------                ----------------
  stdout:  (empty)                 v1 shell helper: COMBINED  -> has run-id
  stderr:  run-id                  v1 stdout-only (SHIPPED BUG): ""  -> lost
           phase/lane lines
           script log() output     v2 execFile: stdout+stderr -> has run-id
```

Any consumer reading only stdout loses the run-id and every `log()` line. The shared builder exists so both arms cannot drift on argv; the combined-output rule exists so neither can drift on streams.

**Objective:** a user on any major agent harness — including surfaces with no
plugin system — can install agentflow and get its real tools plus skill, with
published listings in the registries that have one.

**Means:** one zero-dep stdio MCP server wired through every manifest's
`mcpServers` field (KTD1, KTD2), plus executed external submissions (KTD4).

**Authority:** user-confirmed scope — MCP centerpiece, submissions fired not
just prepped, npm decided-but-deferred to a manual user action.

## Product Contract

### Summary

Ship `agentflow mcp` — a stdio MCP server exposing the runner's tools — wire it
into every plugin manifest's `mcpServers`, execute the remaining registry
submissions, and stage the npm publish path.

### Problem Frame

agentflow only lights up real callable tools on OpenCode. Every other plugin
manifest ships SKILL.md alone — the harness *knows about* the runner but must
shell out blind. And an entire tier (Crush, Cline, Zed-ACP, Roo, Kilo, Kiro)

server collapses N tool implementations into one and reaches every
MCP-capable client, while plugins keep carrying what MCP cannot (skills,
agents/droids, hooks).

- **R1.** `agentflow mcp` answers MCP protocol over stdio — `initialize`,
  `tools/list`, `tools/call` — with no new runtime dependency.

  so a plugin install lights up tools without manual wiring.
- **R3.** The MCP tool surface is `run`, `doctor`, `status`, `tail`, `stop` —
  the verbs an agent needs mid-run. `watch` is excluded (alternate-screen TTY);

# agent-task-queue — serialize expensive ops across parallel agents

## Goal Capsule

Adopt Block's `agent-task-queue` MCP server as the shared chokepoint for expensive operations (builds, test runs, heavy installs) so parallel agentflow workers and concurrent agent sessions stop thrashing the M1 Max — the same pressure that gets `llama-*.service` killed by oomd.

## Product Contract

### The problem

Worker fan-out (`src/pool.mjs`, `agents/worker.md`) can run N agents in parallel, and each may invoke builds/tests freely. On this box, compile + agents together trigger memory pressure → systemd-oomd kills the llama.cpp services (documented known problem). There is no admission control on expensive commands.

### What the tool is

MCP server, `uvx agent-task-queue@latest`. SQLite FIFO queues; `run_task(command, working_directory, queue_name)`; `task_status(task_id, output_offset)` with 30s bounded heartbeats; hierarchical queues (`build/main` exclusive leaves under a shared root); zombie detection kills orphaned children; 120min auto-kill; `--queue-capacity` scopes.

### Scope boundaries

- **In:** install, register in canonical MCP map (dotfiles `.mcp.json` atoms + luke-agents catalog), point agentflow worker builds/tests at a named queue, verify heartbeats + zombie cleanup.
- **Out:** making it *mandatory*. It's a coordination primitive — agents opt in by calling the tool. Enforcement would need the sandboxing plan (separate).
- **Out:** scheduling semantics it doesn't have (priorities, deadlines).

### Requirements

1. Install: `uvx agent-task-queue@latest` — pin a version in the MCP config atom (don't float latest).
2. Queue topology: `shared` root queue for builds/tests; per-worktree leaf queues for anything stateful (`build/<worktree>`).
3. agentflow worker prompt/tool guidance (`agents/worker.md` or the worker spawn path in `src/pool.mjs`): expensive commands (compile/test/install) go through `run_task` on the shared queue.
4. Register in the canonical catalog atom (luke-agents `scripts/mcp/` map) so all harnesses can use it — the value multiplies when Claude/Cursor/Codex sessions share the same queue.
5. Zombie behavior verified: kill a worker mid-task → queued task's process tree dies, queue drains.

### Acceptance examples

- Two concurrent workers both invoke builds → serialized on the queue, second queues instead of racing.
- `task_status` heartbeat returns output offsets mid-build without re-running.
- A killed worker leaves no orphaned `cargo build`/`npm test` processes.

## Repo Touchpoints

- `agents/worker.md`, `droids/worker.md` — worker prompt gets the queue rule
- `src/pool.mjs` — if worker spawn needs to advertise the queue tool
- `docs/` — note in the run/ops docs
- External: luke-agents MCP catalog atom + dotfiles `.mcp.json` entries (committed there, not here)

## Test Scenarios

1. Two queued builds serialize; wall-clock shows no overlap.
2. Heartbeat during a 60s build returns incremental output.
3. Worker SIGKILL mid-task → orphan cleanup, next task starts clean.
4. Non-agent callers (a manual `run_task`) share the same queue as agents.

## Risks / Honest Notes

- Opt-in enforcement is the known hole (upstream README calls this out: permissive Bash rules bypass it). It reduces thrash for cooperative agents only.
- SQLite in /tmp — queue state doesn't survive reboots. Acceptable (queues are ephemeral by nature), but note it.
- 73★, young project. The blast radius is small — worst case, agents route around it and we're no worse than today.

# Worker sandboxing decision — how much isolation do workers get

## Goal Capsule

Decide how agentflow workers (and concurrent agent sessions generally) get isolated: lightweight userspace restriction (`sandbox-runtime`), full kernel-enforced sandbox+gateway (`OpenShell`), or egress-only control now (`smokescreen`) with runtime sandboxing deferred. One decision plan — these are alternatives, not additives.

## Product Contract

### The problem

agentflow workers run generated code and touch real resources — files, network, credentialed MCP tools — with the full ambient authority of the user session. Fan-out makes it N concurrent untrusted-ish processes. Today: zero isolation boundary.

### The candidates

| | sandbox-runtime | OpenShell | smokescreen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boundary | userspace fs/net restrictions | kernel-enforced per-syscall + gateway | egress-only CONNECT proxy |
| Weight | wrap a command | control plane (sandbox+gateway+policy lang) | one Go binary + ACL file |
| Credentials | ambient (real tokens visible) | injected at gateway — agents never hold real tokens | doesn't see creds |
| aarch64 risk | low (TypeScript/OS APIs) | unverified — gate item | low (Go) |
| Telemetry | — | anonymous, on by default (opt-out env) | none |
| Bonus | — | formal verification of policy diffs | per-client ACLs via mTLS identity; SSRF-grade IP blocking |

OpenShell's credential-injection model is the interesting end-state: same philosophy as mcp-oauth-broker (agents never hold raw tokens) extended to every secret.

### Scope boundaries

- **In:** verify each candidate on aarch64/Asahi (hard gate), minimal smoke test wrapping a worker run, decision doc on which layer(s) ship and in what order.
- **Out:** production rollout, policy authoring beyond a trivial allowlist, sandboxing non-agent processes.

### Requirements

1. aarch64 gate first: `sandbox-runtime` install + trivial deny-test; OpenShell support-matrix check (their docs list Linux+Docker — Asahi podman/docker status needs verification). If OpenShell can't run on this box, the decision collapses to sandbox-runtime + smokescreen.
2. Threat-model sentence the decision must answer: are we defending against (a) buggy/hallucinated destructive commands, (b) prompt-injected workers doing exfiltration, or (c) both? (a) → sandbox-runtime suffices; (b) → needs egress control (smokescreen) or OpenShell's gateway.
3. Smoke test: wrap one real agentflow worker invocation in the winner; prove (i) it can still do its job inside the boundary, (ii) a denied action (write outside worktree / fetch a non-allowlisted host) is blocked.
4. Decision doc `docs/decisions/worker-sandboxing.md` with the matrix + chosen order.

### Acceptance examples

- A worker run completes normally inside the boundary (no functionality loss).
- A seeded bad command (`curl evil.example` / `rm` outside worktree) is denied at the layer chosen.
- The doc names the deferred layer explicitly ("smokescreen now, OpenShell when X") rather than leaving it vague.

## Repo Touchpoints

- `docs/decisions/worker-sandboxing.md` (new)
- `src/pool.mjs` / worker spawn path — where the wrap lands (follow-on work after decision)

## Test Scenarios

1. aarch64 install for each candidate — record blockers verbatim.
2. Inside-boundary normal op: worker edits files in its worktree, runs tests — passes.
3. Boundary hit: denied write / denied egress — verify the deny is enforced at the claimed layer.
4. Overhead measure: worker runtime inside vs outside boundary (<10% acceptable for sandbox-runtime).

## Risks / Honest Notes

- OpenShell is the better architecture and the worse first step: control-plane weight, aarch64 unknowns, telemetry opt-out. The honest default is sandbox-runtime + smokescreen now, OpenShell if/when workers touch credentials — which is exactly what the oauth-broker boundary already starts to prevent.
- If ContextForge gateway lands (luke-agents plan), some of OpenShell's value (credential injection, policy) gets partially covered at the MCP layer — the plans interact; the decision doc must say which layer owns what.
- Whatever ships, document the bypass: a user-run command outside the boundary is always possible — this protects agents, not users.

# govern() evaluation — application-layer policy on worker tool calls

## Goal Capsule

Evaluate Microsoft's agent-governance-toolkit — `govern(fn, policy="policy.yaml")` wrapping tool calls with allow/deny/require-approval rules and a tamper-evident audit log — as the *interception-layer* complement/alternative to runtime sandboxing. Output: verdict on whether tool-call governance belongs in agentflow's worker path.

## Product Contract

### The different threat model

Sandboxing (the sibling plan) restricts what the *process* can do. govern() restricts what the *agent* can *invoke* — policy evaluated per tool call, before execution, with denials raising `GovernanceDenied` and every decision logged. Microsoft's framing: prompt-level safety is probabilistic; code-level interception makes bad actions structurally impossible. OWASP Agentic Top 10 coverage.

### Scope boundaries

- **In:** read the toolkit, wrap a representative agentflow worker tool surface (shell, file-write, network-call) with govern() in a scratch harness, exercise allow/deny/approve paths, verdict doc.
- **Out:** adopting it; the full stack (SPIFFE identity, kill-switch SRE, shadow-AI discovery) — eval the core `govern()` + policy + audit first.
- **Relationship to sandboxing plan:** alternatives on the same attack surface; the two plans must reconcile — the verdict doc names which layer owns which defense (likely: govern for tool-call policy + approval gates, sandbox for the subprocess boundary).

### Requirements

1. Scratch wrap: pick one agentflow worker tool path (`src/` shell/exec call, or a worker-invoked MCP tool); apply `govern()` with a YAML policy — deny `rm -rf`, deny network to non-allowlisted hosts, `require_approval` on writes outside the worktree.
2. Exercise the approval path — a denied-by-default action surfaces as an approval request, not a crash.
3. Audit log: verify tamper-evident trail records decision + inputs per call.
4. Verdict doc `docs/decisions/policy-interception-eval.md`: adopt as interception layer | skip (sandboxing covers it) | adopt the *pattern* (own thin wrapper) without the toolkit.
5. If adopt: note Python-interop reality — agentflow is Node (`src/*.mjs`); govern() is Python-first (has TS SDK — check its maturity; if immature, the pattern is borrowable without the lib).

### Acceptance examples

- Deny rule fires: worker attempt at `rm -rf` outside worktree → `GovernanceDenied`, logged, no partial execution.
- require_approval pauses correctly and resumes on grant.
- Audit log survives process restart and is verifiable.

## Repo Touchpoints

- `docs/decisions/policy-interception-eval.md` (new)
- `src/` — only if verdict = adopt (follow-on)

## Test Scenarios

1. allow → executes; deny → blocked + logged; require_approval → pending → approved → executes.
2. Bypass test: worker calls a *non-wrapped* code path — document that govern() sees only wrapped calls (the known blind spot vs runtime sandboxing).
3. TS-SDK viability check on Node 20+.

## Risks / Honest Notes

- The blind spot is structural: anything outside wrapped functions is invisible. A worker spawning a subprocess around the wrap defeats it — which is why this complements, not replaces, process-level isolation.
- MIT, Microsoft-maintained, cross-framework adapters (LangGraph/CrewAI/OpenAI-Agents/ADK/smolagents/Claude-Code plugin). Lowest-risk heavyweight of the three security candidates.
- If both this and sandboxing are adopted, define the layering once: **govern = intent policy, sandbox = capability boundary.** Write that sentence in the doc.

# Chronological parallel build

## Problem frame

The reactor-sim build plan has two long sequential stretches:

1. U6 (Unity control desk) → U7 (Photon Fusion co-op) → U8 (mission arc) ran one after another in the same checkout, each with a 90-minute timeout. U7 took 2h 33m and U8 took 1h 27m on free OpenCode models, giving a ~4h wall-clock tail after all core work was done.
2. Timestamps in agentflow journals and run-ids are UTC (`2026-10-24T03:15:36.533Z`), but the operator console and `agentflow watch` show the bare ISO string. On a machine in `America/Denver` this is 6–7 hours offset and easy to misread.
3. Phases are declared as an ordered list, but the script itself decides what is parallel (`parallel([...])`) and what is serial (`must(await ...)`). There is no first-class dependency graph, so units that could run concurrently wait behind an earlier phase even when their inputs are ready.

## Status key

`done` merged · `in-review` open PR · `planned` not started · `candidate` worth doing only if the stated trigger is met

## Now

### U1. Fan out Unity-side units in reactor-sim-build.mjs
- **Status:** planned. Evidence: the current script at `reactor-sim/.agentflow/workflows/reactor-sim-build.mjs` runs U6, then U7, then U8 serially with a shared checkout.
- **Dependencies:** `worktree: 'auto'` already lands in M6; `phase()` journal records already land in the watch-view work.
- **Approach:**
  - Run U6 serial first because U7 and U8 both extend `PlantBridge.cs` and the panel.
  - Run U7 and U8 in `worktree: 'auto'` parallel worktrees.
  - Add an `integrate-unity` phase that merges the two worktrees into master and reconciles `PlantBridge.cs`.
  - Give U7 and U8 different starting models so they do not both hammer the same free-tier provider.
- **Verification:** a fresh run of `reactor-sim-build.mjs` shows U7 and U8 in parallel in `agentflow watch`, wall time for the Unity tail drops to `max(U7, U8) + integration` instead of `U7 + U8`.

- **Feasibility:** high. U7 and U8 produce mostly non-overlapping files (`Net/` vs `Missions/`, `MissionEngine.cs` vs `SimStateSync.cs`). The only shared files are `PlantBridge.cs` and possibly `PanelReadout.cs`; the integrator resolves those.

- **Status:** candidate. Trigger: another build with more than one long serial tail.

  ```mjs
  export const meta = {
    phases: ['u6', 'u7', 'u8', 'integrate-unity'],
    deps: {
      u7: ['u6'],
      u8: ['u6'],
      'integrate-unity': ['u7', 'u8'],
  ```

# Landscape: who else orchestrates agents, and where agentflow sits

Gathered 2026-10-10. Sources are fetched pages or `gh api` lookups made that
day (URLs inline). Claims about agentflow come from the code at `origin/main`
(`eb5ef35`) and the two open PRs (#7, #8), not from the README. This extends,
and in places corrects, `cross-harness-dynamic-workflows.md` (2026-10-08) and
`orchestration-economics.md` (2026-10-09).

## 1. What "cross-harness" means in this code

It is narrower and more concrete than the marketing sentence suggests.

- A **harness** is an agent CLI that can run one prompt non-interactively:
  `devin -p`, `claude -p`, `codex exec`, `opencode run`, `ori code -p`
  (`src/adapters/*.mjs`). One more adapter, `openrouter`, is not a harness at
  all: an in-process `POST /chat/completions` with no tools; `echo` is a test
  stub.
- The **adapter contract** is small: `buildArgv(spec)`, `parse(result, spec)`,
  optional `buildEnv`, `permissionDeniedPatterns`, `probe()`, and an optional
  `spawnAgent` override (`src/adapters/base.mjs`). `spawnAgent` spawns the
  process with `stdio: ['ignore', ...]`, enforces timeout and abort, and
  classifies failure.
- The **portable unit is the workflow script**: one `.mjs` file using the
  globals `agent / parallel / pipeline / phase / log / args`. The same file
  runs under any adapter, selected by `--harness`. `agent()` resolves to
  `{text, json}` or `null`, so scripts are harness-neutral by construction.
- **Per-harness normalisation** is where the work is: permission modes map to
  each CLI's flag (`escalated` becomes `bypassPermissions` for claude,
  `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for codex); `schema` is native
  only on codex (`--output-schema`) and prompt-level elsewhere; `worktree` is
  native on codex only until PR #8 adds a runner-provisioned `'auto'` mode.
- **`--via ori`** is a second axis: the same harness binary is wrapped as
  `ori <harness>` so model routing and billing go through OpenRouter
  (`applyVia`). This makes `claude`/`codex`/`opencode` workers runnable on
  non-Anthropic/OpenAI models. Not available for `devin`.
- Not cross-harness: sessions, tool permissions, MCP config and context are
  not shared. Workers share only the filesystem (the SKILL.md says so). The
  coordination substrate is the journal (`.agentflow/runs/<id>.jsonl`), not a
  protocol like ACP or A2A.
- Verified by use, not just code: the 2026-10-09 live matrix
  (`docs/smoke-matrix.md`) got `PONG` from all six real rows, and the matrix
  found a real bug (codex bypassing `applyVia`).

So: "cross-harness" = *one script, a thin per-CLI argv/parse adapter, and an
optional OpenRouter wrapper*. That is the whole claim, and it is a real one.

## 2. Comparable systems

| System | What it is | Better than agentflow | Worse / different | Source |

## 3. What users expect (from the comparables)

1. **Resume that does not redo finished work.** Temporal replays from history;
   Claude replays by prompt order and reruns from the first differing prompt.
   Agentflow replays by call index only (`runtime.mjs`: `prior.settled.has(i)`),
   with no prompt check, so an edited script silently reuses stale results.
   This is the biggest correctness gap against expectation.
2. **A way to watch a run.** Claude has `/workflows`; LangGraph has LangSmith.
   Agentflow has `status` and `tail` (a journal poller) and `--detach`.
3. **Determinism enforced, not advised.** Temporal and Claude both enforce it.
   Agentflow now shadows `Date`, `Math` and `crypto` by default, with
   `--allow-nondeterminism` to opt out. The old `--strict` regex lint is gone.
4. **Structured output that is validated.** Claude retries up to five times on

5. **Cost and token visibility.** Claude shows per-agent token use; agentflow

6. **Safe-by-default permissions and an escape hatch.** Already modelled in

7. **Saved/shareable workflows.** Claude: `.claude/workflows/` and plugin

## 1. The Claude reference implementation, verified

  optional `model` routing, optional `worktree` isolation.

  excess work queues.
- Env: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` overrides all agent models;

- Built-in: `/deep-research`. Triggers: ask for a workflow, the `ultracode`

Ori is OpenRouter's agent launcher + native coding agent, installed here.

- **`ori code`** — Ori's own agent loop, headless-capable:

# Interrupt-safe journaling for pooled subprocess agent runs

## Context

agentflow fans out one-shot harness CLIs (`devin -p`, `claude -p`, `codex exec`,
`opencode run`) under a bounded pool and journals each settled call to JSONL so
`--resume` can replay results and re-execute only unsettled work. Two interrupt
races silently break that contract if journaling happens "after" the task:

1. **Journal-after-release race.** If a task releases its in-flight slot in
   `finally` and the settle continuation journals afterward, a SIGINT drain can
   observe "nothing in flight" and write `run-end` + exit before the finished
   result is appended. Work completes but is never recorded — resume re-runs it.
2. **Abort-masquerading-as-failure.** An in-flight call killed by our own
   `AbortController` returns an ordinary failure shape. If that is journaled as
   a settled failure, resume replays it as a *result* (`null`) instead of
   re-executing the call — the run quietly loses work.

## Guidance

- **Journal inside the pool task, before releasing the slot.** The invariant is
  `inFlight.empty ⇒ durable record`. Any ordering where slot-release precedes
  the append is unsafe under drain.
- **Classify your own abort.** A failure that lands while `abort.signal.aborted`
  is a cancellation, not a settled result — do not journal it. Resume must see
  it as unsettled so it re-executes.
- **Queued-vs-settled is a journal question, not a queue question.** Drained
  queue items resolve `null` without a record; only genuinely-executed calls are
  journaled.
- **Gate normal completion on an in-progress signal handler.** If the script
  finishes while drain is still waiting on grace, the process must still exit
  with the signal code (130/143) and after the `run-end` record — otherwise the
  run reports success with dropped calls.
- **Detect headless permission stalls.** Non-interactive harness sessions that
  hit an approval prompt exit nonzero with recognizable stderr; adapter-supplied
  `permissionDeniedPatterns` regexes keep that distinct from ordinary agent
  failure so operators see "needs `permission: 'escalated'`" rather than "agent
  failed".

## Verified headless flag matrix (2026-10-09, this machine)

| Harness | Spawn | Model | Structured output | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| devin | `devin -p <prompt> --respect-workspace-trust false` | `--model` | prompt-level only | `--permission-mode dangerous` |
| claude | `claude -p <prompt> --output-format json` | `--model` | prompt-level (envelope `.result`) | `bypassPermissions` |
| codex | `codex exec <prompt>` | `-m` | `--output-schema <file>` native | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` |
| opencode | `opencode run <msg> --format json` | `-m provider/model` | prompt-level (event JSONL) | `--auto` |

Gotchas worth the bytes:

- Devin's `--permission-mode auto` is read-only — too weak for coding agents;
  `smart` is the useful default.
- `devin plugins install` prompts interactively; `-y` is required headless.
- Codex needs `--skip-git-repo-check` outside git dirs and writes the final
  answer via `-o <file>`, not stdout.
- OpenCode `--format json` emits an event stream (JSONL) — the answer is the
  concatenation of text parts, not the last line.
- Private repos on the free GitHub tier cannot receive branch protection via
  API — `gh repo create` hardening silently degrades there.

## Why This Matters

Resume correctness is the difference between "workflow runner" and "script that
re-runs everything." The failure modes above are invisible in happy-path tests —
they only appear under interrupt — and each one silently converts real agent
work into either duplicated cost or permanently lost results.

## When to Apply

- Any orchestrator spawning processes with a kill/resume lifecycle.
- Any wrapper that translates a harness's approval model into headless calls.

# The via-wrap contract: every spawnAgent must route through applyVia

## What happened

`--via ori` wrapping lived in the generic `spawnAgent` in
`src/adapters/base.mjs`. Codex overrides `spawnAgent` (it needs a temp dir for
`--output-last-message` + `--output-schema` files) and called `spawnProcess`
directly — so `--via ori` silently produced a **bare** codex invocation with an
OpenRouter model slug: `codex exec -m z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` → exit 1. Found only
by the live smoke matrix; no test caught it because the argv-unit tests
exercise `buildArgv`/`applyVia`, not the override path.

## The invariant

Any adapter that overrides `spawnAgent` must still run
`applyVia(this, buildArgv(...), spec)` and honor `wrapped.error`. The wrap is
not decoration — it rewrites the binary (`argv[0]` becomes ori's subcommand),
moves model routing to ori's `--model`, and injects `--reasoning-effort`.
Skipping it is not a degraded mode; it produces a *wrong binary invocation*.

Two failure shapes this prevents:

- **Silently direct:** credentials/model billed to the wrong provider
  (subscription instead of OpenRouter, or an OR slug rejected by the native
  provider — codex's case).
- **Leaked native flag:** adapter's `-m`/`--model` forwarded untouched into a
  harness that doesn't know OpenRouter slugs.

## Test guidance

Argv-level tests can't see into a custom `spawnAgent`. The catch that works is
the live smoke matrix (`docs/smoke-matrix.md`) — every adapter × `--via ori`
must produce a real `PONG`. If an adapter gains a custom `spawnAgent`, add the
`applyVia` call and re-run that row.

## Related findings worth keeping

- Codex's session header prints `provider: openai` even when ori routes to
  OpenRouter — it's a generic OpenAI-compatible label, not evidence of
  misrouting.
- `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` returns `empty completion` intermittently under burst
  concurrency (~5/12 calls in one deep-research run). Tolerated as `null`;
  a retry-on-empty opt is a candidate follow-up.
